families.label: Instrumental variables
families.definition: An instrument that shifts the treatment but affects the outcome only through it identifies the effect for those whose treatment the instrument moves.

families.label: Difference in differences
families.definition: The change in the outcome of a treated group is compared with the change of an untreated group over the same period; parallel trends do the identifying work.

families.label: Event study
families.definition: Outcomes are traced before and after an event at the individual level, so pre-event trends are visible and the effect is read from the post-event deviation.

families.label: Regression discontinuity
families.definition: A rule assigns treatment at a threshold of a running variable; units just above and just below the cutoff are compared.

families.label: Fixed effects (within variation)
families.definition: Time-invariant differences between units are removed by comparing each unit with itself over time or across its own members.

families.label: Sibling and family comparison
families.definition: Siblings or other family members are compared with one another, holding everything shared within the family fixed.

families.label: Twin comparison
families.definition: Twins are compared with one another, holding shared genes and upbringing fixed.

families.label: Matching
families.definition: Each treated unit is paired with untreated units that look alike on observables, and their outcomes are compared.

families.label: Selection on observables
families.definition: Treated and untreated units are compared after adjusting for observed characteristics, assuming nothing unobserved drives both treatment and outcome.

families.label: Randomised controlled trial
families.definition: Treatment is assigned at random by the researchers or a programme, so the treated and the untreated are alike in expectation.

families.label: Lottery
families.definition: Treatment is allocated by an actual lottery outside the researchers' control, such as an admission or housing lottery.

families.label: Bunching
families.definition: The mass of units piling up at a kink or notch of an incentive schedule reveals the behavioural response to the incentive.

families.label: Synthetic control
families.definition: A weighted combination of untreated units is built to track the treated unit before treatment; the gap afterwards is the effect.

families.label: Structural model
families.definition: An economic model is estimated and its parameters, not a reduced-form contrast, carry the causal content.

families.label: Other designs
families.definition: Designs that fit none of the families above.

families.label: Descriptive
families.definition: No identification strategy is claimed; the estimate describes an association or a gap.

sub_designs.label: Field experiment
sub_designs.definition: Randomisation by the researchers in the field.

sub_designs.label: Randomised policy pilot
sub_designs.definition: A programme randomised by the implementing agency.

sub_designs.label: Survey or laboratory experiment
sub_designs.definition: Randomisation inside a survey or laboratory setting.

sub_designs.label: bunching at a reference point
sub_designs.definition: Excess mass in the distribution of an outcome at a salient behavioural reference value, rather than at a policy-created kink or notch, relative to a counterfactual distribution.

sub_designs.label: bunching in non-manipulable measure
sub_designs.definition: Excess mass at the threshold is measured in a third-party-reported version of the running variable that units cannot themselves misreport, isolating real responses from reporting responses.

sub_designs.label: clustering of group modes at kink
sub_designs.definition: Instead of individual excess mass, the design asks whether group-level modes of the outcome distribution pile up at the threshold.

sub_designs.label: Bunching at a kink
sub_designs.definition: Excess mass at a kink of the schedule.

sub_designs.label: mass in dominated region
sub_designs.definition: The share of units choosing an option strictly dominated by the tax or subsidy schedule measures inattention or frictions rather than preferences.

sub_designs.label: Bunching at a notch
sub_designs.definition: Excess mass and a hole around a notch of the schedule.

sub_designs.label: placebo kink for unaffected group
sub_designs.definition: Excess mass is measured at a kink for a group whose own marginal rate does not change there, as a falsification of the bunching design.

sub_designs.label: reform-shifted kink in schedule
sub_designs.definition: A reform moves the kink point and changes its rate, so the shift in the earnings distribution between pre- and post-reform cross-sections identifies the behavioural response.

sub_designs.label: birth-order exposure gap across families
sub_designs.definition: The within-family difference between an earlier- and a later-born sibling, who by birth order spend different amounts of early childhood with a younger sibling, is compared across families in which the younger sibling's condition occurred and families in which it did not.

sub_designs.label: Continuous exposure (dose-response)
sub_designs.definition: Units differ in the intensity of exposure to the change rather than in a treated/untreated split.

sub_designs.label: expiry of time-limited policy
sub_designs.definition: Eligible and ineligible units are compared before and after a time-limited policy lapses at its fixed duration limit.

sub_designs.label: gender gap across environment groups
sub_designs.definition: The difference in outcomes between boys and girls, which arises from the randomness of child gender, is compared across groups of families defined by parental education or marital status, differencing out level effects of gender and of environment.

sub_designs.label: high versus low exposure groups
sub_designs.definition: Units are split into high- and low-exposure groups by predicted treatment intensity and their outcomes are compared before and after a common shock date.

sub_designs.label: matched event-time treatment and control
sub_designs.definition: Units experiencing an event at a given date are compared over event time with observationally matched units that do not experience the event in that or adjacent periods.

sub_designs.label: measurement-scheme gap across groups
sub_designs.definition: The same units are scored under two assessment schemes and the gap between groups is differenced across the two schemes.

sub_designs.label: placebo-timed never-treated control group
sub_designs.definition: Units experiencing an actual event are compared over event time with never-event units to whom placebo event dates are assigned from the treated units' observed timing distribution.

sub_designs.label: policy change with sibling controls
sub_designs.definition: A dated policy change that affects one family member but not their siblings identifies its effect by comparing within families across cohorts exposed before and after the change.

sub_designs.label: Staggered adoption
sub_designs.definition: Units are treated at different dates; later-treated units serve as controls for earlier ones.

sub_designs.label: Triple difference
sub_designs.definition: A second untreated dimension removes group-specific shocks from the difference in differences.

sub_designs.label: two-period health shock versus controls
sub_designs.definition: The change in an outcome between a pre-shock and a post-shock period is compared between individuals hit by a health shock and comparable unaffected individuals.

sub_designs.label: Two-period policy change
sub_designs.definition: One reform at one date; treated and untreated groups before and after.

sub_designs.label: two-period shock change versus unchanged controls
sub_designs.definition: Groups defined by how an individual-level exposure changes between two consecutive periods are compared with the group whose exposure stays untreated in both periods, differencing out pre-existing level differences.

sub_designs.label: continuous dosage leads and lags
sub_designs.definition: A continuous within-unit measure of treatment intensity is entered at leads and lags around its changes, net of unit and period-by-group fixed effects, to trace the dynamic response of the outcome.

sub_designs.label: Family event
sub_designs.definition: The event is a birth, a marriage or another change in the family.

sub_designs.label: firm-level shock to fixed cohort
sub_designs.definition: Workers are grouped into cohorts by their pre-shock employer and tracked after that employer receives a shock, so cohort composition is fixed before the shock.

sub_designs.label: Individual shock
sub_designs.definition: The event is a shock to the individual: job loss, illness, death of a relative, divorce.

sub_designs.label: Policy change
sub_designs.definition: The event is a reform or rule change at a known date.

sub_designs.label: pretreatment trend test around shock date
sub_designs.definition: Interactions of exposure with pre-period dummies test whether differentially exposed units were already trending apart before the shock date.

sub_designs.label: quasi-random visit timing around recommendation
sub_designs.definition: Identification rests on quasi-random variation in the exact week of a routine universal service visit relative to a fixed nationally recommended date, with the event study run around that visit week.

sub_designs.label: Firm or establishment fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Each firm or workplace is compared with itself over time.

sub_designs.label: Individual fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Each person is compared with themself over time.

sub_designs.label: job-spell fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Worker-firm job-spell fixed effects absorb all time-invariant characteristics of the match, so only within-spell changes in the firm's exposure identify the effect.

sub_designs.label: Mover design
sub_designs.definition: Units that move between places, firms or regimes identify place or firm effects.

sub_designs.label: municipality fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Units are compared within cells defined by their municipality of residence, so that all between-municipality differences are absorbed.

sub_designs.label: occupation-trait interaction within job spells
sub_designs.definition: Within job-spell variation in exposure is interacted with predetermined occupation characteristics, so identification comes from differential responses across occupations with different temporal flexibility rather than from the individual's own choices.

sub_designs.label: own-gender interaction within cohort cells
sub_designs.definition: Peer composition is interacted with the student's own gender inside school-by-cohort fixed-effect cells, so identification rests on how the same cohort's composition affects men and women differently.

sub_designs.label: parent-child pair fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Variation is taken within a fixed parent–child pair over time, absorbing the pair's persistent common component.

sub_designs.label: peer composition within institution cells
sub_designs.definition: Units in the same institution-by-characteristic cell are exposed to differently composed sets of peers, and the cells are absorbed by fixed effects so only the quasi-random variation in peer exposure remains.

sub_designs.label: school fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Students differing in treatment are compared only within the same school, so that all school-level unobservables are differenced out.

sub_designs.label: Two-way fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Unit and time fixed effects together.

sub_designs.label: Distance or access
sub_designs.definition: Distance to, or local availability of, a service or institution instruments its use.

sub_designs.label: Health or mortality shock
sub_designs.definition: An illness or death, treated as unforeseeable, instruments a change in circumstances.

sub_designs.label: historical value of treatment as instrument
sub_designs.definition: A predetermined historical measurement of the treatment variable, fixed long before the outcome, is used as an instrument for its contemporaneous value.

sub_designs.label: independent second measurement as instrument
sub_designs.definition: An independently collected second measurement of the same latent, mismeasured regressor is used as its instrument, so that classical measurement error in the regressor is purged from the estimated relationship.

sub_designs.label: instrumental variables.firm closure as exogenous job loss
sub_designs.definition: Unanticipated closure of the employing firm is used as an instrument that imposes unemployment independently of the worker's own choices.

sub_designs.label: Judge or caseworker leniency
sub_designs.definition: The leniency of the randomly assigned decision-maker instruments the decision taken for the individual.

sub_designs.label: local population size as instrument
sub_designs.definition: The naturally varying, predetermined size of the population living in a unit's surrounding area instruments the unit's own size.

sub_designs.label: Lottery or random assignment as instrument
sub_designs.definition: A lottery or random assignment instruments actual take-up of the treatment.

sub_designs.label: nearby openings and closings as instrument
sub_designs.definition: Administratively decided openings and closings of neighbouring institutions generate sudden, politically driven changes in a unit's size that serve as the instrument.

sub_designs.label: Other instrument
sub_designs.definition: An instrument of another kind.

sub_designs.label: Peer or network exposure
sub_designs.definition: Exposure of peers or network members to a shock instruments the individual's treatment.

sub_designs.label: Policy eligibility rule
sub_designs.definition: A rule that makes some units eligible for a programme instruments participation.

sub_designs.label: quasi-random fertility shock
sub_designs.definition: A chance biological fertility outcome (success of a fertility treatment, twin conception) that is as good as random conditional on treatment circumstances serves as the instrument.

sub_designs.label: Shift-share (Bartik) instrument
sub_designs.definition: Exposure of units to aggregate shifts, weighted by their initial shares, instruments the local change in the treatment.

sub_designs.label: Simulated (mechanical) policy instrument
sub_designs.definition: A mechanically simulated change in the treatment variable, computed by applying new policy rules to baseline (pre-period) behavior, instruments the actual change in treatment.

sub_designs.label: Timing of birth or cohort
sub_designs.definition: The month or year of birth relative to a rule instruments the treatment, such as school starting age.

sub_designs.label: Weather or natural shock
sub_designs.definition: A natural event such as rainfall, temperature or a disaster instruments the treatment.

sub_designs.label: random sibling sex
sub_designs.definition: The sex of a later-born sibling, unknown to parents at conception, is treated as a natural lottery that assigns units a brother or a sister.

sub_designs.label: Exact or coarsened matching
sub_designs.definition: Matching on the values, or coarsened values, of chosen covariates.

sub_designs.label: matched comparison group
sub_designs.definition: Treated units are paired with untreated units on observed characteristics to form a comparison group, without a specified propensity-score or exact-cell rule.

sub_designs.label: Propensity score matching
sub_designs.definition: Matching on the estimated probability of treatment.

sub_designs.label: age-period-cohort decomposition with trend restriction
sub_designs.definition: Age, period and cohort dummies are estimated jointly with the two collinear linear trends allocated by an explicit identifying restriction, so the non-linear age, period and cohort components of the outcome are read off directly.

sub_designs.label: before-after in independent data source
sub_designs.definition: The same policy date is examined in an outcome measured by an independent source that is unaffected by the reporting behaviour under study.

sub_designs.label: before-after versus reference group
sub_designs.definition: The before-after change at a policy date for the affected population is compared with that of a reference group not subject to the mechanism at issue.

sub_designs.label: before-after without control group
sub_designs.definition: Outcomes for a single population are compared immediately before and after a policy date, with no untreated comparison group.

sub_designs.label: causal mediation via sequential ignorability
sub_designs.definition: The effect of a quasi-exogenous variable is decomposed into a path through an intermediate variable that is assumed conditionally random given pre-treatment and intermediate confounders.

sub_designs.label: cohort contrast in conditional association
sub_designs.definition: The conditional association between a predictor and an outcome is compared between an earlier cohort and a later cohort that made the same decision under different circumstances, with no exogenous variation in the predictor itself.

sub_designs.label: decomposition of group gap into components
sub_designs.definition: The observed gap between two groups is split into a part accounted for by differences in measured characteristics and an unexplained residual attributed to differences in returns, without any exogenous variation.

sub_designs.label: descriptive mapping without counterfactual
sub_designs.definition: A conclusion is drawn from a descriptive mapping of the observed activities and remits of the actors present in a setting, with no comparison group.

sub_designs.label: designed Monte Carlo with known truth
sub_designs.definition: Data are simulated from a data-generating process whose parameters and sample dimensions are set by the authors, so an estimator's deviation from the known truth is observed directly.

sub_designs.label: experimenter-set parameters across rounds
sub_designs.definition: Treatment conditions are set by the experimenter and applied uniformly to all subjects in each round, so within-subject comparisons across rounds identify their effects even without randomised ordering.

sub_designs.label: interrupted time series trend break
sub_designs.definition: The outcome series is regressed on a linear time trend plus an indicator for the policy period, so the effect is the break from the extrapolated trend.

sub_designs.label: measurement-month versus other months
sub_designs.definition: Behaviour is compared between the calendar month in which the rule-relevant variable is measured and the other months of the year, optionally against a group not subject to the rule.

sub_designs.label: Other
sub_designs.definition: A design of another kind.

sub_designs.label: other.miscarriage delayed comparison group
sub_designs.definition: Women who were pregnant equally early but whose first birth was delayed by a miscarriage serve as the comparison group for early childbearers, the health event rather than choice producing their later birth.

sub_designs.label: predicted-effect accounting
sub_designs.definition: Previously estimated elasticities are applied to observed changes in exposure to compute predicted outcome changes across the distribution, without new identification.

sub_designs.label: qualitative thematic coding of interviews
sub_designs.definition: Explanations are inferred from thematically coded interview accounts of actors in the setting, with no exogenous variation and no counterfactual comparison.

sub_designs.label: quasi-random sibling gender comparison
sub_designs.definition: Identification comes from the quasi-random gender of a sibling, which is treated as an as-good-as-random family draw for comparing units or splitting the sample.

sub_designs.label: quasi-random sign of small balance
sub_designs.definition: Units with a small positive versus a small negative balance around a zero threshold are treated as quasi-randomly assigned, and outcomes are compared across the sign of the balance.

sub_designs.label: selection-correction exclusion restriction
sub_designs.definition: Identification rests on a variable that shifts the probability of being observed in the sample but is excluded from the outcome equation, used to correct selection.

sub_designs.label: timing-of-events duration model
sub_designs.definition: Identification comes from the timing of treatment entry within an ongoing spell, with the treatment-entry and outcome durations modelled jointly and selection absorbed by correlated time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity.

sub_designs.label: Age or date cutoff
sub_designs.definition: The running variable is age or a calendar date.

sub_designs.label: Fuzzy cutoff
sub_designs.definition: The probability of treatment jumps at the threshold; the jump instruments treatment.

sub_designs.label: Sharp cutoff
sub_designs.definition: Treatment switches deterministically at the threshold.

sub_designs.label: conditional random policy placement
sub_designs.definition: Units are placed into locations by an administrative allocation rule that overrides their own preferences, so the characteristics of the location they receive are as good as randomly assigned conditional on the attributes the administrator observes.

sub_designs.label: measurement-source comparison
sub_designs.definition: Two alternative measures of the same underlying condition for the same individuals are each used to predict the outcome, and the gap between the predictions is interpreted as measurement bias.

sub_designs.label: observed trait with randomized stimulus
sub_designs.definition: Units differing in an observed, non-randomized characteristic are compared on their response to a stimulus whose attributes are randomized, so the stimulus is held constant by design rather than by control.

sub_designs.label: Regression adjustment
sub_designs.definition: Covariates enter a regression; the treatment coefficient is the estimate.

sub_designs.label: respondent versus non-respondent comparison
sub_designs.definition: Units that selected into the survey sample are compared with those that did not, using characteristics and outcomes observed for the whole sampling universe, to assess response-based selection.

sub_designs.label: Reweighting
sub_designs.definition: Untreated units are reweighted to resemble the treated on observables.

sub_designs.label: selection on observables.predetermined measure long before outcome
sub_designs.definition: Treatment is measured long before the outcome is observed, so the cross-sectional association, conditional on covariates, cannot be driven by reverse causality or by shocks moving both at the same time.

sub_designs.label: sequential confounding adjustment over time
sub_designs.definition: Identification comes from adjusting for all observed common causes measured repeatedly at each time-point, so that time-varying treatment is as good as randomly assigned within confounder histories.

sub_designs.label: sequential covariate-block gap adjustment
sub_designs.definition: A predetermined group indicator is regressed on the outcome with blocks of covariates entered in sequence, so the shrinking group coefficient shows how much of the raw gap each block accounts for.

sub_designs.label: soon-to-be-treated comparison group
sub_designs.definition: Units that have just experienced an event are compared, conditional on observed covariates, with units that will experience the same event shortly after the outcome is measured.

sub_designs.label: Extended family comparison
sub_designs.definition: Cousins or other relatives compared within the extended family.

sub_designs.label: sibling family comparison.sibling fixed effects with miscarriage delayed sister
sub_designs.definition: Sisters are compared within the same family where the non-early-childbearing sister's first birth was delayed by a miscarriage, so the family fixed effect absorbs background while the health event supplies the timing variation.

sub_designs.label: Sibling fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Siblings compared within the family.

sub_designs.label: additive extrapolation to unvalued states
sub_designs.definition: Parameters estimated on directly valued profiles are summed additively to predict the value of a profile that was not itself directly valued.

sub_designs.label: coherent multi-population mortality forecast
sub_designs.definition: A multi-population (coherent) mortality forecasting model is fitted to observed death rates by sub-population and then used to evaluate outcomes under alternative statutory policy schedules.

sub_designs.label: counterfactual policy reform simulation
sub_designs.definition: An estimated structural model is re-solved under a hypothetical policy rule to predict behaviour under that reform.

sub_designs.label: Dynamic discrete choice
sub_designs.definition: A dynamic programming model of choices estimated on the data.

sub_designs.label: finite mixture of unobserved types
sub_designs.definition: Persistent unexplained differences in outcomes within unit-state cells allocate units to a finite set of unobserved types, whose type-specific productivities are then identified from units observed in several states.

sub_designs.label: general equilibrium counterfactual simulation
sub_designs.definition: An estimated and calibrated equilibrium model is re-solved under a counterfactual path of an exogenous variable, holding idiosyncratic draws fixed, and simulated outcomes are compared with the baseline solution.

sub_designs.label: hybrid additive utility model from valuation tasks
sub_designs.definition: A parametric additive utility model is estimated jointly on two experimentally assigned valuation task formats to recover attribute-level utility parameters.

sub_designs.label: Life-cycle model
sub_designs.definition: A model of consumption, saving, labour supply or schooling over the life cycle.

sub_designs.label: long panel lifetime earnings benchmark
sub_designs.definition: Identification comes from an auxiliary panel long enough to observe the full-horizon measure directly, against which a short-horizon proxy is benchmarked.

sub_designs.label: multiple reports with partial validation
sub_designs.definition: Covariances among three or more reports of the same mismeasured quantity, only one of which is assumed error-free and only for part of the sample, identify the components of measurement error.

sub_designs.label: observed history versus model forecast
sub_designs.definition: The historically observed trajectory of an outcome is contrasted with the trajectory implied by a fitted forecasting model under the policy schedule, with no comparison group in the data.

sub_designs.label: preference parameters from budget kinks
sub_designs.definition: Structural utility parameters are recovered from how units respond to sharp kinks in the budget set they face.

sub_designs.label: production function with investment proxy
sub_designs.definition: A production function is estimated by inverting the firm's investment policy function to proxy for unobserved productivity, which is assumed to follow a Markov process.

sub_designs.label: production function with labor aggregation
sub_designs.definition: Estimates a production function in which heterogeneous labor groups are aggregated into efficiency units, so that cross-firm variation in workforce composition recovers each group's relative marginal product.

sub_designs.label: Search or matching model
sub_designs.definition: A labour market search or matching model.

sub_designs.label: static random-utility location choice
sub_designs.definition: A static discrete-choice (logit) model of choosing among spatial alternatives is imposed on an observed cross-sectional choice matrix, with its parameters recovered from the distribution of chosen alternatives.

sub_designs.label: structural model.panel covariance restrictions
sub_designs.definition: Identification from covariance restrictions on panel moments of income and consumption growth, which separate permanent from transitory components and their pass-through to spending.

sub_designs.label: structural model.simulated parameter grid experiment
sub_designs.definition: Steady-state equilibria of the estimated structural model are simulated over a grid of structural parameters and an econometric estimator is applied to the simulated panels to study its behaviour.

sub_designs.label: Sufficient statistics
sub_designs.definition: A formula from theory combines estimated elasticities into a welfare or policy effect.

sub_designs.label: validation measure assumed error-free
sub_designs.definition: A second, administrative measurement of the same quantity is assumed to be the true value, so the survey–validation discrepancy directly identifies the measurement-error parameters.

sub_designs.label: within-family correlation restrictions
sub_designs.definition: Variances of shared human-capital factors are recovered from a system of within-family education correlations (spouse, parent-child, sibling) closed by restrictions on which factors each type of family pair shares.

sub_designs.label: Synthetic control
sub_designs.definition: A donor pool weighted to match the treated unit before treatment.

sub_designs.label: Twin fixed effects
sub_designs.definition: Twins compared within the pair.

sub_designs.label: Regression kink
sub_designs.definition: The slope, not the level, of the treatment changes at the threshold.

sub_designs.label: Geographic boundary
sub_designs.definition: The running variable is distance to a border between regimes.

sub_designs.label: Nearest-neighbour matching
sub_designs.definition: Matching on a distance over covariates.

sub_designs.label: Admission lottery
sub_designs.definition: Oversubscribed school or programme places allocated by lottery.

sub_designs.label: Allocation lottery
sub_designs.definition: Housing, land or other goods allocated by lottery.

sub_designs.label: Other structural model
sub_designs.definition: A structural model of another kind.

patterns.label: Differences in X across units, conditional on observed covariates, identify X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: Treatment varies across units in the cross-section and identification rests on controlling for observed characteristics, with no unit fixed effects to absorb unobserved heterogeneity.

patterns.label: Variation in X within units over time, net of unit and unit-by-period fixed effects, identifies X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: Unit and period (or unit-by-period) fixed effects absorb level differences and common shocks so that only within-unit, over-time variation in the treatment identifies the outcome response.

patterns.label: The timing of a shock to the individual (job loss, illness, death) identifies its effect on Y
A rule assigns X at a threshold of a running variable; Y is compared across the cutoff
Units experience differently sized changes in X over time; Y is compared across units and periods
patterns.definition: Identification comes from differential, continuously measured changes in the treatment across units over time, with outcomes compared across units and periods.

patterns.label: Units differing in X within the same institution are compared on Y, holding the shared institution fixed
patterns.definition: Identification comes from comparing units that differ in X but share the same institution, so institution-level unobservables cannot drive the difference in Y.

patterns.label: A shift in exposure to X across units instruments X's effect on Y
Estimated structural parameters are used to compute the model-implied response of Y to a counterfactual change in X
patterns.definition: Parameters estimated from observed behaviour are fed back into the model, which is solved or evaluated with and without a hypothetical change in the treatment, and the difference in simulated outcomes is the estimated effect.

patterns.label: Equilibrium model matched to observed moments
patterns.definition: An equilibrium model linking X to Y is estimated by matching auxiliary moments of observed behaviour, and X's effect on Y is recovered from the estimated structural parameters.

patterns.label: Policy date event study
patterns.definition: A policy takes effect at a known date and Y is traced period by period around that date for units exposed to X relative to unexposed units.

patterns.label: Family members differing in X are compared on Y, holding the shared family fixed
A mechanical change in X predicted by applying changed policy rules to baseline behavior instruments X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: Policy rules are applied to units' base-period characteristics to compute the change in X they would mechanically experience, and this simulated change instruments the observed change in X in estimating its effect on Y.

patterns.label: A policy reaches units at different dates; Y is compared around each unit's date
X is allocated at random; Y is compared between the allocated and the rest
Excess mass at a kink identifies elasticity
patterns.definition: A discontinuous change in the marginal incentive X at a kink in a schedule creates excess mass in the distribution of Y around the kink, and the size of that excess mass relative to a smooth counterfactual density identifies Y's elasticity with respect to X.

patterns.label: Varying structural parameters in model simulations
patterns.definition: X is varied over a grid in simulations from an estimated model, and Y is computed from the simulated data to trace X's effect on Y.

patterns.label: X becomes available to one group at a policy date; Y is compared between that group and an unaffected group across cohor
patterns.definition: A single dated policy change makes a treatment available to one group but not another, and the group gap in the outcome is compared across cohorts (or periods) before and after that date.

patterns.label: A jump in X at a threshold of Y produces excess mass in Y just above the threshold and missing mass just below, identify
patterns.definition: A discrete change in the schedule of X at a threshold of the outcome variable creates bunching above and a hole below the threshold relative to a smooth counterfactual density, identifying behavioural responses to X.

patterns.label: A policy change raises exposure to X for one group at a given date; Y is compared between exposed and unexposed units be
patterns.definition: A dated policy change increases a treatment or exposure for an identifiable group of units, and outcomes are compared between exposed and unexposed units before versus after the change.

patterns.label: A quasi-random biological event that shifts X instruments X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: A chance biological event that moves units into or out of X, independent of their histories, instruments X's effect on Y.

patterns.label: Two way fixed effects variance decomposition
patterns.definition: Units observed in several groups let Y be decomposed into additive unit and group components X, identified by units that move between groups under exogenous mobility.

patterns.label: Variation in X across groups, periods and a third dimension, net of all double interactions, identifies X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: Treatment intensity varying jointly along three dimensions is used after absorbing every main effect and two-way interaction, so only the residual three-way variation in X identifies Y.

patterns.label: An independent second measurement of the same mismeasured X instruments X's effect on Y
patterns.definition: A second, independently measured proxy of the same latent treatment variable serves as the instrument for the mismeasured treatment, identifying X's effect on Y net of classical measurement error.

patterns.label: A policy change restricts X for one group at a given date; Y is compared between that group and an unaffected group befo
patterns.definition: Identification comes from a dated policy change that binds only one identifiable group, with the before-after change in the outcome for that group differenced against the contemporaneous change for a group the rules leave untouched.

patterns.label: Moments of x and y growth over varying horizons identify responses to permanent and transitory components of x
patterns.definition: Variances of X growth and its covariance with Y growth over lengthening horizons separate permanent from transitory components of X and identify the response of Y to each.

units.source_of_variation: random assignment of the stratified sample of about 42,800 taxpayers to a 100% audit group and a 0% audit group for tax returns filed in 2007, implemented by SKAT

units.summary: Cross-person differences in register-recorded hospital diagnoses over the preceding four years are related to planned retirement age, with identification resting on conditioning on a rich set of economic, job and background controls (plus selection corrections) rather than on any exogenous shock.

units.summary: Changes in a worker's register-recorded diagnoses between survey waves are compared with changes in that same worker's planned retirement age, so time-invariant individual unobservables are differenced out.

units.source_of_variation: Comparison of two alternative measures of the same condition for the same individuals: the survey self-report and the register hospital-discharge diagnosis. No reform, lottery or instrument is used.

units.summary: Employees assigned by pre-reform (2008) income to a group whose net-of-tax rate rose 18 percent are compared with just-below-cutoff employees whose rate barely changed, and the 2009-to-2010 difference in income change is scaled by the difference in net-of-tax rate changes to recover the shifting response.

units.summary: Monthly payroll records let the paper trace, month by month around the reform's announcement and effective date, the wage income of high-rate employees relative to employees with negligible rate change, so the dip before and spike after January 2010 identifies intertemporal shifting.
units.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, proposed 1 March 2009, passed 28 May 2009 and effective 1 January 2010, cut the marginal tax rate on labor income for high-wage earners from 62.8 to 56.0 percent, creating an incentive to postpone wage payments from 2009 into 2010; employees with negligible incentive form the control group.

units.summary: Identification comes from fitting an equilibrium search model with sorting by indirect inference to 57 auxiliary statistics on mobility, unemployment durations and wages conditional on a firm's poaching rank, assuming the poaching index ranks firms by productivity and all workers agree on that ranking.
units.source_of_variation: Firm-rank conditional worker mobility and wage patterns in Danish matched employer-employee data 1994-2003: firms are ranked by the poaching index (the fraction of a firm's hires poached from other firms), and 57 auxiliary statistics on rank-conditional mobility, unemployment durations, re-employment wages and log-wage moments are matched by Indirect Inference. No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used.

(1999) two-way fixed effects decomposition), applied to the Danish data and to data simulated from the estimated structural model.

units.source_of_variation: Numerical experiment: steady-state equilibria of the model are solved and simulated over a grid of (rho, beta) combinations, and the log-additive wage equation (B1) is estimated on the simulated panels; no register data are used.

units.summary: A series of small tax reforms is used to build a simulated two-year change in each person's net-of-tax rate, holding income and characteristics at their base-year values, and this mechanical change instruments the actual net-of-tax rate change in an earnings-growth regression.

units.summary: The same individuals previously observed at the top kink are followed to the smaller middle kink two years later, so excess mass at the smaller kink is compared holding fixed individual characteristics.

units.summary: Excess mass is measured at the middle tax pension kink, which shares the near-zero scope of the top pension kink but has a much smaller rate change, isolating the role of kink size from that of kink scope.
units.source_of_variation: the middle tax pension kink, which has the same near-zero scope as the top tax pension kink but a much smaller size, isolating size from scope

units.source_of_variation: the location of the statutory top tax cutoff in the wage earnings distribution, compared with the distribution of occupation-level modes around it

units.source_of_variation: the pension kink: for workers at the cap on tax-deductible pension contributions the top tax starts about DKr 33,000 above the statutory cutoff, giving a kink of the same size but near-zero scope

units.summary: Bunching at the statutory top tax cutoff is measured in the realized income distribution of self-employed individuals, for whom the marginal tax rate does not change at that point, as a check on what drives the observed mass.
units.source_of_variation: the statutory top tax cutoff, studied on self-employed individuals whose own marginal tax rate does not change there

units.summary: The jump in the marginal tax rate at the Danish top-bracket cutoff creates a kink in the budget set, and the excess mass of self-employed income piled at that cutoff relative to a smooth counterfactual density estimated from adjacent bands identifies the taxable-income elasticity.
units.source_of_variation: The discrete jump in the marginal tax rate at the top tax bracket cutoff of the Danish piecewise linear personal income tax schedule, which creates a kink in the budget set; bunching of the income distribution at that kink identifies the behavioural response.

units.source_of_variation: Approval of lithium in 1976, with separate interactions for each two-year birth cohort 1946-1976 (1953-54 omitted)

units.summary: Labour market outcomes are traced in event time around the date of a person's first registered psychiatric diagnosis between 1995 and 2015, documenting (descriptively) how earnings, nonemployment and disability evolve before and after onset.
units.source_of_variation: Timing of a person's first psychiatric diagnosis recorded in the register between 1995 and 2015

units.source_of_variation: Approval of lithium as a maintenance treatment for BD in 1976, compared within families (people with BD versus their siblings)

units.summary: People diagnosed with bipolar disorder, depression or schizophrenia are compared with their undiagnosed siblings, differencing out shared family background to describe the career gap associated with diagnosis.
units.source_of_variation: Within-family differences in diagnosis status between people with a mental health disorder and their healthy siblings

units.summary: Because lithium approval in 1976 was relevant only for bipolar disorder, the change in the bipolar outcome gap across the 1956 cohort cutoff is differenced against the corresponding change for people with depression or schizophrenia, who the approval did not affect.
units.source_of_variation: Approval of lithium in 1976 for BD only, with people with depression or schizophrenia as a second control group (triple difference)
