units.summary: Monthly contribution rates of earners just above the top-bracket threshold, whose deduction value fell with the announced reform, are compared before and during the announcement year against earners just below the threshold whose marginal rate was practically unchanged.
units.source_of_variation: The 2010 Danish tax reform, passed by parliament on 28 May 2009 and taking effect on 1 January 2010, which lowered the marginal tax rate for top-bracket taxpayers from almost 63% to 56% while leaving it practically unchanged for others; because pension contributions are tax deductible, this created a temporary incentive during the announcement period of 2009 to advance contributions while the deduction rate was still high. Identification compares employees above the DKK 35,000 monthly 2008 earnings cut-off (T-group) with employees earning DKK 30,000-35,000 (C-group) over the 48 months January

units.summary: Whether the first IVF cycle with embryo implants succeeds is treated as quasi-random given age, treatment year and education, so it instruments motherhood and additional births for earnings, participation and hours.
units.instrument: IVF treatment success at the first IVF treatment with embryo implants
units.source_of_variation: success versus failure of the first IVF treatment with embryo implants among childless women, treated as a natural experiment

units.summary: Intention-to-treat effects of a successful first IVF cycle are estimated by comparing successful and unsuccessful women conditional on age at treatment, treatment year, education and pretreatment outcome averages.
units.source_of_variation: success versus failure of the first IVF treatment with embryo implants among childless women, treated as a natural experiment

units.summary: Among successfully treated IVF women with at least two implanted embryos, whether the implants yield twins rather than a singleton is taken as biologically exogenous and instruments family size for earnings.
units.instrument: twins at first birth (indicator of a singleton versus twin birth)
units.source_of_variation: twin versus singleton birth among successfully treated IVF women who received at least two embryo implants

atlas.from_label: Distance of the prison placement from home

units.summary: In a representative sample of Danish mothers, the chance occurrence of twins at first birth instruments the number of children to estimate its effect on labor earnings as a benchmark for the IVF estimates.
units.instrument: twins at first birth (indicator of a singleton versus twin birth)
units.source_of_variation: twin versus singleton birth at first birth among a representative sample of Danish mothers

units.summary: Income losses of displaced relative to nondisplaced workers are differenced again across displacements occurring before versus after the 1989 decentralization of sectoral wage bargaining, so the change in the displacement penalty at the reform identifies the effect of decentralized bargaining.
units.source_of_variation: The January 1989 renegotiations between DI and CO-metal that decentralized wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector, combined with the timing of mass-layoff displacements before versus after that reform; displaced workers are compared with nondisplaced workers within each period.

atlas.from_label: decentralization of the wage bargaining system

units.summary: Displaced workers with above-median predisplacement wages, who were most exposed to firm-level wage setting, are compared with below-median displaced workers before versus after the 1989 reform, so differential exposure to decentralization identifies its effect on postdisplacement wage losses.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in displacement timing before versus after the January 1989 wage bargaining reform, interacted with whether the displaced worker's predisplacement wage was above the median.

atlas.from_label: decentralization of the wage bargaining system

units.summary: Within displaced workers, variation in elapsed time since displacement and in postdisplacement tenure, net of worker fixed effects and age, identifies wage recovery profiles, estimated separately for pre- and post-reform displacements.
units.source_of_variation: Within-worker variation in elapsed time since displacement and in postdisplacement tenure among displaced workers, estimated separately for workers displaced before and after the January 1989 reform.

atlas.from_label: decentralization of the wage bargaining system

units.summary: Event-study paths of wages, unemployment and earnings around displacement, relative to nondisplaced workers, are traced separately for cohorts displaced before and after the 1989 bargaining reform, and the gap between the two sets of paths identifies the reform's effect.
units.source_of_variation: The January 1989 renegotiations between DI and CO-metal that decentralized wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector, combined with the timing of mass-layoff displacements before versus after that reform; displaced workers are compared with nondisplaced workers within each period.

units.summary: The timing of separation during a firm-level mass layoff or closure, plausibly unrelated to the individual worker, is used to trace income paths relative to observationally comparable nondisplaced workers.
units.source_of_variation: Mass-layoff separations (firm workforce contraction of more than 30% from one observation year to the next, or establishment closure) in Danish manufacturing, compared with nondisplaced workers in the same equidistant subsample.

units.summary: The same displacement event study is run in the finance and banking sector, whose bargaining system was not decentralized, so the absence of a post-1989 change in displacement losses there supports the manufacturing design.
units.source_of_variation: Mass-layoff displacements in the Danish finance and banking sector, a sector whose wage bargaining system was not decentralized in a comparable way in the early 1990s; used as a placebo for the manufacturing reform.

units.summary: The displacement event study is repeated for low-skilled SID union members who largely remained under the standard wage rate system after 1989, a group with weak exposure to decentralization, as a check on the main comparison.
units.source_of_variation: Mass-layoff displacements among low-skilled SID union members, many of whom remained under the standard wage rate system after 1989; used as a placebo group with weaker exposure to the decentralization reform.

units.summary: A new national parental-leave entitlement available only to parents whose youngest child was aged 0-8 lets the paper compare the change in health care workers' leave-taking and employment from 1993 to 1994-96 between eligible and ineligible parents, attributing the differential jump to the reform.
units.source_of_variation: The federally funded Danish parental-leave program introduced on 30 June 1993 and effective 1 January 1994, which offered any parent up to one year of absence per child aged 0-8, combined with predetermined differences in the fertility and child-age distribution of health care workers across counties and sectors in 1993

units.summary: Predetermined 1993 differences in nurses' fertility and child-age composition across county-sector health care markets predict how much the 1994 leave reform mechanically reduced nurse staffing, and this exposure-times-post term instruments county-level nurse employment in equations for elderly patient mortality and readmission.
units.instrument: Exposure_c^s x I_{94-96}: predicted county-sector parental-leave take-up among nurses in hospitals interacted with an indicator for the post-reform years 1994-96
units.source_of_variation: The federally funded Danish parental-leave program effective 1 January 1994 interacted with predetermined county-sector differences in the fertility and child-age distribution of nurses in 1993

units.summary: Workers moving between establishments within the largest connected set identify additive person and establishment effects in an AKM decomposition of log wages and hours, and the average establishment effect is compared between women and men to measure sorting.
units.source_of_variation: Movement of workers between establishments within the largest connected set identifies the establishment effects; the reported number contrasts the female and male populations' average exposure to those effects.

atlas.from_label: sorting of women into lower-hours workplaces

units.summary: The same AKM establishment effects identified from worker mobility are normalised by assuming zero average effects for low value-added-per-worker firms, so that the level of establishment pay premia and their contribution to the gender gap can be read off in the accounting-data subsample.
units.source_of_variation: Worker mobility between establishments identifies the AKM establishment effects; the normalisation assumes average establishment effects are 0 for firms with value added per worker below an estimated threshold.

units.summary: The gender gap is measured as the average male-female difference in residuals from year-by-year log wage regressions controlling for age, experience, occupation, education and establishment, i.e. a descriptive adjustment for observables with no exogenous variation.
units.source_of_variation: Residual from year-by-year log wage regressions including age fixed effects, a cubic in experience and occupation, education and establishment indicators; no exogenous variation.

units.summary: The 1987 dual-income-tax reform raised the net-of-tax interest rate on mortgage debt far more for top-bracket taxpayers than for those below, so comparing housing outcomes of top-bracket and below-top taxpayers before and after 1987 identifies the response to the deduction's value.
units.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which introduced dual income taxation and taxed negative capital income at the bottom rate. It raised the net-of-tax interest rate on negative capital income by 81 percent for the top bracket, 29 percent for the middle bracket, and lowered it by 6 percent for the bottom bracket.

units.summary: Denmark's post-1987 house price path is compared with a weighted combination of donor countries matched on pre-reform prices, so the divergence after the reform measures its aggregate price effect.
units.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, a national policy change affecting about half of the Danish population, compared against countries that had no such reform.

units.summary: Families whose member suffers a first-time nonfatal heart attack or stroke in year tau are compared with families whose member suffers the same shock in year tau+5, so that only the as-good-as-random year of the shock within a five-year window distinguishes treated from not-yet-treated controls.
units.source_of_variation: The year, within a five-year window, in which a family member suffers a first-time nonfatal heart attack or stroke: family members of individuals shocked in year tau are compared with family members of individuals shocked in year tau + 5.

units.summary: Among bereaved households, those whose family member died of the condition under study are compared over time with those whose member died of another cause, so the shared bereavement effect is differenced out and only the condition-specific behavioral response remains.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the cause of death across treated (bereaved) households: individuals whose family member died of the studied disease x are compared with those whose family member died of another cause.

units.summary: Households bereaved in year tau are compared with households bereaved in year tau+5, treating the exact year of the death within the five-year window as as-good-as-random given cohort, age and calendar year.
units.source_of_variation: The year, within a five-year window, in which a family member dies: families bereaved in year tau are compared with families bereaved in year tau + 5.

units.summary: The jump in deductions claimed between the last self-reporting year and the first pre-populated year is read as the effect of third-party reporting, since the reform hit all taxpayers at one date and surrounding years were flat.
units.source_of_variation: Raw before/after comparison of administrative tax-register aggregates around the 2008 introduction of third-party information reporting and pre-population for charitable deductions; the paper states it has no control group.

units.summary: Within a sample of taxpayers almost certainly eligible for a deduction, the paper regresses pre-reform claiming on taxpayer characteristics and other self-reported items with demographic controls, treating the conditional differences as reporting behaviour rather than differences in giving.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation across taxpayers in the indicator of interest, within a sample of high-propensity donors who are very likely to have had an eligible charitable deduction in 2007, conditioning on demographic controls.

units.summary: The reform-year change in the number of claims by size bin is compared between taxpayers with accountancy training, who face record-keeping costs but no information friction, and the rest of the population.
units.source_of_variation: Before/after comparison of the number of charitable deductions claimed by claim-size bin around the 2008 reform, split between taxpayers with accountancy training and the rest of the population; accountants serve as a frame of reference with the same record-keeping costs but no information friction.

units.summary: Annual growth in the number and value of charitable deductions is regressed on a linear trend and a reform-year dummy, so the effect is the one-year deviation from trend in a series with no control group.
units.source_of_variation: Interrupted time series: annual growth in the number of deductions claimed regressed on a linear time trend and an indicator for 2008, the year third-party information reporting for charitable deductions was introduced. The paper states there is no control group because the reform hit all taxpayers at once.

units.summary: Donor counts and donation values filed by the largest charities, a source independent of taxpayer reporting, are tracked around the reform date to show that actual giving did not jump when claimed deductions did.
units.source_of_variation: Before/after comparison of charity-reported donor counts around the 2008 introduction of information reporting, using an independent data source (charities' own annual compliance filings) that is unaffected by taxpayers' reporting behaviour.

units.summary: A random sample of taxpayers was audited without prior announcement under the pre-reform self-reporting regime, so the audited returns reveal the population rate of overclaimed charitable deductions.
units.source_of_variation: An unannounced large-scale randomized audit experiment conducted in 2007 on 2006 tax returns (Kleven et al., 2011); the audit reveals true liabilities for a random sample.

units.summary: Because the audits were unannounced and randomly assigned, the rate at which auditors uncovered unclaimed deductions in the random sample can be benchmarked against the share of eligible deductions the reform implies went unclaimed.
units.source_of_variation: An unannounced large-scale randomized audit experiment conducted in 2007 on 2006 tax returns (Kleven et al., 2011); its detection of missing deductions is compared with the number implied by the reform-based estimate that about half of all eligible deductions were unclaimed.

units.summary: Among taxpayers with a small preliminary balance, whether it falls just above or just below zero owed taxes is treated as quasi-random and learned only after the tax year, so claiming rates on each side reveal reporting responses to owing money.
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of a small preliminary tax surplus or deficit (|amount| below DKK3,000) around the zero owed-taxes threshold, following Engstrom et al. (2015); claiming behaviour is compared across the threshold.

units.summary: The pre-2012 subsidy threshold makes second and later gifts just below DKK500 strictly dominated, so the density of gifts in that range measures how many donors are unaware of the giving incentives.
units.source_of_variation: The kinked-and-notched charitable subsidy scheme in place before 2012: with a one-third subsidy and a DKK500 eligibility threshold, second and subsequent gifts in [DKK333, DKK500) are strictly dominated. The density of gifts in that region measures a lack of awareness of the incentive.

units.summary: A dummy for having a GPA at or above the lowest published standby admission threshold among the listed programmes instruments actual admission, so that applicants just above and just below the cutoff identify the local effect of being admitted on degree completion.
units.instrument: d = 1[r >= 0], a dummy for the applicant's GPA being equal to or above the standby admission threshold of the first-choice programme
units.source_of_variation: Discontinuity at the lowest standby GPA admission threshold among the programmes listed on the application, used as an instrument for admission to any listed programme

units.summary: Admission is granted mechanically once GPA reaches the first-choice programme's standby threshold, which varies by programme and year and is published only after applications are filed, so outcomes are compared just above versus just below that cutoff.
units.source_of_variation: Discontinuity at the standby GPA admission threshold of the first-choice programme: all applicants with a GPA above the published threshold are admitted, the threshold varies across programmes and across application years 1994-2002, and it is published only after all applications have been submitted

units.summary: Using the lowest standby threshold among all programmes listed on the application as the cutoff, applicants whose GPA just clears it are compared with those just below to identify effects on admission anywhere and completion of any degree.
units.source_of_variation: Discontinuity at the lowest standby GPA admission threshold among the higher degree programmes listed on the application; thresholds vary by programme and application year and are published only after applications are submitted

atlas.from_label: admission to one of the higher degree programmes listed on the application

units.summary: The first-choice programme's Quota 1 GPA threshold for direct admission provides the discontinuity, with applicants just above and just below it compared on direct admission, enrolment and degree completion.
units.source_of_variation: Discontinuity at the Quota 1 GPA admission threshold of the first-choice programme (direct admission via Quotas 1 or 2)

units.summary: Event-study child penalties for women are compared across quintiles of their maternal grandparents' relative labor supply, conditioning on grandparental education, wealth rank, region and birth cohort so that the remaining cross-sectional variation is treated as unrelated to other determinants of the penalty.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional variation across quintiles of the relative labor supply (cumulated hours 1964-1979) of the grandparents; child penalties themselves come from the event study

atlas.to_label: Gender gap in earnings from children

units.summary: Outcomes are tracked in event time around the individually varying date of the first birth, with age and year dummies and men as a comparison group, so the sharp break at the birth is attributed to children under smoothness.
units.source_of_variation: individual-level variation in the timing (year) of the first childbirth, with men used as the comparison group for women; age and calendar-year dummies absorb lifecycle and time trends

units.summary: Parents' earnings around their first birth are differenced against the earnings of individuals who never have children, who are given placebo birth dates drawn from the parents' age-at-first-birth distribution, so common lifecycle paths net out.
units.source_of_variation: timing of the first childbirth for parents relative to placebo birth timing for individuals who never have children

units.summary: Comparing same-gender twins raised in the same household, the twin-pair fixed effect absorbs shared genes and family environment so that the within-pair difference in educational attainment identifies education's effect on later criminal convictions.
units.source_of_variation: Differences in educational attainment within same-gender twin pairs raised in the same childhood household; the twin pair fixed effect absorbs genetic, environmental and familial factors common to the two twins.

units.summary: Cross-sectional differences in educational attainment across individuals, adjusted only for birth-cohort dummies (and juvenile crime), give an association between education and crime that the paper itself presents as non-causal.
units.source_of_variation: None: cross-sectional variation in educational attainment across individuals, with birth cohort dummy variables only. The paper presents these as associations and states they fail to deal with the endogenous relationship between education and crime.

units.summary: Cancer patients are compared with same-gender, same-age, same-base-year individuals without cancer, assuming that conditional on observed baseline characteristics (with propensity-score overlap) diagnosis is unrelated to potential labour market outcomes.
units.source_of_variation: incidence of a first cancer diagnosis (any ICD-10 C code except skin cancer) in 2000-2005 recorded in the Danish cancer register, compared with individuals of the same gender, age and base year without cancer; in Table B7 the control group consists of persons first diagnosed six years later

units.summary: Identification comes from differencing each person's outcome between two years before and four years after the diagnosis year and comparing that change for cancer patients with the change for matched individuals without cancer, assuming common trends.
units.source_of_variation: incidence of a first cancer diagnosis (any ICD-10 C code except skin cancer) in 2000-2005 recorded in the Danish cancer register, compared with individuals of the same gender, age and base year without cancer

units.summary: The parent's time-averaged after-tax earnings (or family disposable income) is instrumented with the Danish mean earnings of the parent's gender-by-three-digit-occupation cell, so that only the systematic, occupation-level component of parent income drives the intergenerational elasticity and attenuation from transitory measurement error in parent income is purged.
units.instrument: Mean earnings in Denmark by gender and three-digit occupational code
units.source_of_variation: No policy or natural experiment: the parent's time-averaged after-tax earnings is instrumented with the mean earnings in Denmark by gender and three-digit occupational code, in order to remove attenuation bias from measurement error in parent earnings.

units.summary: The parent's registry-imputed permanent consumption is instrumented with the same parent's self-reported expenditures from the Danish Expenditure Survey, an independent measurement of the same latent consumption, so the consumption mobility elasticity is identified under classical, mutually uncorrelated measurement errors in the two sources.
units.instrument: Log self-reported consumption (expenditures) of the parent from the Danish Expenditure Survey
units.source_of_variation: No policy or natural experiment: the imputed permanent consumption of the parent is instrumented with the same parent's self-reported consumption from the Danish Expenditure Survey, an independently measured proxy for the same latent consumption, so as to remove the attenuation bias that imputation and measurement error would otherwise induce.

units.summary: The first stage of the same design shows how strongly the parent's survey-reported expenditures co-move with the registry-imputed permanent consumption, establishing that the two independent sources measure the same latent parental consumption and that the instrument is relevant.
units.instrument: Log self-reported expenditures of the parent (the excluded instrument whose first-stage strength is reported here)
units.source_of_variation: The two measures of the same parent's consumption come from different sources -- a self-reported expenditure survey and an imputation from administrative registry proxies -- and the first stage documents how strongly they co-move.

units.summary: Reversing the roles of the two measurement sources, the parent's self-reported survey consumption is used as the regressor and the long-run registry proxies (mean home and car values) as its instruments, which identifies the consumption elasticity even when imputation errors are serially correlated, provided parent-proxy and child-imputation errors are mutually uncorrelated.
units.instrument: The mean value of the home and the mean value of the cars of the parents over the 15-year sample period (the dental-care and total-expenditure proxies are excluded as weaker instruments)
units.source_of_variation: The roles of instrument and proxy are reversed relative to the main estimator: the self-reported survey consumption of parents becomes the regressor and the registry proxies (mean home value and mean car value over 15 years) become the instruments, which makes the estimator consistent even under positive serial correlation in the imputation error.

units.summary: Identification comes from idiosyncratic year-to-year swings in the female share of a high school's entry cohort, which survive school fixed effects, cohort fixed effects and school-specific trends and cannot be anticipated by applicants, so peer gender composition is as good as randomly assigned within a school over time.
units.source_of_variation: Idiosyncratic year-to-year variation in the proportion of female students within Danish general academic high schools across entry cohorts 1980-1994, after taking out school fixed effects, cohort fixed effects and school-specific time trends.

atlas.to_label: probability of enrolling in STEM programs

units.summary: With school-by-cohort fixed effects absorbing everything common to a cohort, the peer female share is interacted with the student's own sex, so the estimate is the differential response of men and women exposed to the very same cohort composition.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the proportion of female peers combined with the student's own gender within cohort-by-school cells, so the coefficient identifies how the peer gender composition differentially affects men and women within the same school cohort.

units.summary: A randomization check that regresses the leave-out female peer share on the student's own sex within school-by-cohort cells, controlling for the school-level leave-out mean to purge the mechanical link, confirming that cohort gender composition is unrelated to who the student is.
units.source_of_variation: Student's own gender within school-by-cohort cells; a randomization check in the spirit of Guryan, Kroft, and Notowidigdo (2009).

units.summary: Year-to-year movements in the female share of one track of a high school cohort are related to the share in the other track of the same cohort, showing that the composition variation used for identification is a school-cohort-level shock rather than track-specific sorting.
units.source_of_variation: Year-to-year variation in the female share across the two tracks of the same high school cohort.

units.summary: Exposure to the 2010 cap on deductible annuity contributions, assigned by whether pre-reform contributions exceeded the threshold, instruments the induced fall in annuity saving and traces how each lost krone reappears in other pension saving or mortgage repayment.
units.instrument: Treat_i x Post_i,t
units.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, which made employer-paid plus individual contributions to annuity pension schemes tax-deductible only up to DKK 100,000; individuals with 2008 annuity contributions above the threshold are treated, those below are non-treated.

atlas.from_label: tax incentives for saving in annuity pension schemes
atlas.to_label: Exposure to peers in other crime types

units.summary: Individuals contributing above the new deductible ceiling before the reform are compared with those below, before and after 2010, so the differential change in annuity contributions measures the reform's effect under common pre-reform trends.
units.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, which made employer-paid plus individual contributions to annuity pension schemes tax-deductible only up to DKK 100,000, here replaced by a placebo reform in 2008, a year with no reform.

atlas.from_label: tax incentives for saving in annuity pension schemes

units.summary: Interacting treated status with year indicators traces the year-by-year probability of shifting saving from annuity to life-long schemes, with flat pre-reform coefficients showing no anticipation and the post-reform jump dating the response to the cap.
units.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform capping tax-deductible annuity pension contributions at DKK 100,000; Treat_i is interacted with year indicators.

atlas.from_label: tax incentives for saving in annuity pension schemes
atlas.to_label: Exposure to peers in other crime types

units.summary: Within the experiment, individual background characteristics (nationality, gender, age) are related to evasion in a double-hurdle regression that conditions on the experimental parameters and the other covariates, so identification rests on conditional ignorability of these observed traits.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in measured individual characteristics across the 180 participants, conditioned on the other regressors of the double-hurdle model.

units.summary: The tax rate, audit probability and redistribution regime are fixed by the experimenter and identical for all subjects in each of the nine rounds, so within-subject variation in these parameters across rounds identifies their average effect on declared income.
units.source_of_variation: Experimenter-controlled within-subject variation in the tax rate, the audit probability and the redistribution regime across the nine rounds of the experiment (Table 1, p. 186). The order of stages and rounds was deliberately NOT randomised.

units.summary: Singles with immigrant background, whose right to bring a foreign spouse into Denmark was curtailed by the 2002 reform, are compared with otherwise similar citizens of immigrant background not bound by the new rules, before versus after 2002, in yearly emigration to Sweden.
units.source_of_variation: The 2002 Danish family reunification reform, announced in January 2002 and passed in June 2002 (in force from 1 July 2002), which introduced the 24-year rule, the attachment requirement, an adequate-housing requirement, a financial-support requirement on the sponsor and a bank collateral of 63,413 DKK - compared across single Danish citizens with immigrant background (treated) and Danish citizens with immigrant background cohabiting or married with a non-EU citizen (control), before and after 2002.

units.summary: The half-yearly count of reform-affected couples moving into Sweden is modelled as a stable pre-2002 trend plus level and slope breaks at the Danish reform date (with additional break terms for the Oresund Bridge opening and a lagged 2003 response), so the effect comes purely from the timing of the break in the series.
units.source_of_variation: Interrupted Time Series Analysis of the half-yearly number of affected in-migrants to Sweden around the Danish 2002 family reunification reform (announced January 2002, passed June 2002); identification rests solely on time-series variation. The paper explicitly chose ITSA over a regression discontinuity in time design.

units.summary: Yearly emigration rates to Sweden are plotted for the reform-affected group and the unaffected comparison group around 2002, so that visibly parallel pre-reform paths and a post-reform divergence identify the reform's effect.
units.source_of_variation: The 2002 Danish family reunification reform; Fig. 3 is the graphical difference-in-differences comparing yearly emigration rates of the treatment and control group before and after 2002 (vertical line at the reform year).

units.summary: Treatment and control membership is frozen as of 2001 and survival in Denmark is tracked from that date, so the divergence in Kaplan-Meier emigration hazards after the 2002 reform reflects the policy rather than compositional change in group membership.
units.source_of_variation: The 2002 reform, with survival time measured from 2001 for a fixed treatment and control group defined before the reform - a robustness check against selection into and out of the groups.

units.summary: The same before-after comparison of affected and unaffected citizens is run for emigration to Germany instead of Sweden, so the absence of a reform response there supports the claim that Sweden is the relevant alternative destination.
units.source_of_variation: The 2002 Danish family reunification reform, with Germany as the alternative destination - a falsification-style comparison supporting the argument that Sweden, not Germany, is the attractive alternative.

units.summary: The half-yearly inflow into Sweden of couples affected by the Danish reform is compared around 2002 with the inflow of the same type of couples arriving from Finland and Norway, whose reunification rules did not change, so the reference series absorbs common Swedish-side shocks.
units.source_of_variation: Interrupted Time Series Analysis (Eq. 3) comparing the half-yearly number of affected in-migrants from Denmark with the same type of couples arriving from Finland and Norway, around the Danish 2002 family reunification reform.

units.summary: Workers with high tenure who lose their job when their firm sheds at least 30% of its peak employment are followed in event time relative to the layoff, with individual and municipality-by-year fixed effects, so the jump in crime after the sudden, unanticipated separation identifies the displacement effect.
units.source_of_variation: firm-level mass layoffs between 1990 and 1994 -- a 30% decline in firm employment relative to the firm's peak over the previous five years, for firms with 30 workers or more -- hitting high-tenure workers who are unlikely to separate otherwise; identification is within municipality and year

units.summary: Successive labor-market acts changed the statutory length of passive and active benefit entitlement, and because they took effect on fixed dates they hit the 1990-1994 displacement cohorts at different points of their post-displacement spell, so crime is tracked around the legislated transitions between benefit regimes.
units.source_of_variation: the 1993 Act on an Active Labor Market (Lov 434 of June 30, 1993), the Executive Order Lbk 16 of January 11, 1994 (4 years of passive and 3 years of active benefits) and the amendment Lbk 29 of January 23, 1996 (passive period cut to 2 years), which hit the 1990-1994 displacement cohorts at different points of their post-displacement spell and so shift the statutory timing of benefit periods cohort by cohort

units.summary: Displacement-event indicators from the mass-layoff design instrument labor and total income, while legislated year-to-year changes in the maximum unemployment benefit instrument nonlabor income, under the Beckerian assumption that these shocks affect crime only through income.
units.instrument: pre- and post-displacement event indicators for labor earnings
units.source_of_variation: job displacement during firm mass layoffs in 1990-1994 as an instrument for labor (or total) income, and policy-induced shifts in the legislated maximum unemployment benefit amount (127,608 DKK in 1990-1991, 132,600 DKK in 1992, 137,020 DKK in 1993, 132,340 DKK in 1994-1996) as an instrument for nonlabor income

units.summary: Displaced workers are sorted into fifteen equally sized bins of post-displacement labor earnings and compared on crime within worker and year, so that the pre-displacement year and the worker fixed effect absorb prior income, giving a within-worker earnings-crime gradient rather than a causal estimate.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional differences in labor earnings across displaced workers in the two years around displacement, within worker and year

units.summary: Current convictions of high-tenure workers who will later be displaced are compared with those of co-workers at the same employer, municipality and year, conditioning on age, tenure, wage, education, industry, firm size and marital status, to see whether displacement is selected on unobserved criminal propensity.
units.source_of_variation: comparison, within the same employer, municipality and year, of the current convictions of high-tenure workers who will be displaced in some y0 between 1990 and 1994 with those of workers who will not

units.summary: Crime is regressed on income over the thirteen years around displacement with worker fixed effects and municipality-by-time fixed effects, so only within-worker income movements net of local shocks are used to trace the income-crime relationship.
units.source_of_variation: within-worker variation in income over the 13 years around displacement, net of municipality-time shocks

units.summary: Because the 1998 reform applied retroactively to children born after a fixed date, couples whose first child arrived just after the cutoff got two earmarked paternity weeks while otherwise-similar couples giving birth just before did not, so comparing the two cohorts' household income shares over time (with household fixed effects) identifies the reform's effect.
units.source_of_variation: The April 1998 reform of the Danish parental leave system, which entitled all fathers of children born after October 15, 1997 to two additional earmarked weeks of paternity leave; first births within one year after the reform (treated) are compared with first births within one year before the reform (control).

units.summary: The post-reform birth indicator is interacted with years-since-first-birth dummies, tracing how the woman's income share of treated couples evolves relative to the pre-reform cohort before and after the birth.
units.source_of_variation: The April 1998 reform of the Danish parental leave system (two additional earmarked weeks of paternity leave for fathers of children born after October 15, 1997), with the treatment effect interacted with dummies for years since the first birth.

units.summary: A fictitious reform date in a year with no change to earmarked paternity leave rules is fed through the baseline specification, so a null effect on the woman's income share supports the identifying assumptions of the main design.
units.source_of_variation: An artificial (placebo) reform date of October 15, 2003 / implementation in 2004, used to test the baseline design; the year is chosen because there was another reform in 2002.

units.summary: Municipalities approve their first preschool in different years, so cohorts born in the same municipality differ in whether a preschool existed when they were three; comparing outcomes across municipality-by-birth-cohort cells net of municipality and birth-year fixed effects identifies the effect, and crossing this rollout with the independently staggered nurse home visiting rollout identifies the
units.source_of_variation: municipality x birth-year variation in the timing of the first government approval of a preschool across the 138 Danish municipalities that ever had an approved preschool by 1960, over the 1933-1960 rollout, combined with the independent municipality x birth-year variation in the rollout of the Nurse Home Visiting program (approvals 1937-1949)

units.summary: Within municipalities that eventually approve a preschool, cohorts differ only in how old they were when the approval happened, and outcomes are traced across these age-at-approval indicators to show effects appear for cohorts young enough to attend and not for older ones.
units.source_of_variation: variation in the cohorts' age at the time of the first preschool approval in their municipality of birth, among municipalities that approve a preschool between 1934 and 1960

units.summary: The first-stage effect on actual attendance is identified by comparing interpolated enrollment shares in municipality-by-year cells before and after a municipality has at least one approved preschool, net of municipality and year fixed effects.
units.source_of_variation: municipality x year variation in the presence of at least one approved preschool among urban ever-implementing municipalities, 1939-1950

units.summary: The same municipality-by-birth-year rollout variation is applied to fertility and composition outcomes to check that approval timing is not accompanied by changes in the number or selection of births that generate the cohorts being compared.
units.source_of_variation: municipality x birth-year variation in the timing of the first government approval of a preschool across the 138 ever-implementing municipalities, 1933-1960

units.summary: Identification comes only from municipalities that switch from no preschool to an approved preschool during the sample window, so treated cohorts are compared with cohorts from the same switching municipalities rather than with never-implementing areas.
units.source_of_variation: municipality x birth-year variation in preschool approval restricted to municipalities that change treatment status during the sample period

units.summary: Firm (or establishment) fixed effects absorb time-invariant heterogeneity so that estimated year effects trace changes in firms' internal spatial organization among surviving firms that opened, closed or reallocated workers across establishments, rather than changes in the composition of firms entering and exiting.
units.source_of_variation: Within-firm (or within-establishment) variation over time: firms that opened and/or closed establishments, or reallocated workers across them, in each year of 1981-2016, net of the entry and exit of different types of firms

units.summary: Switching costs are recovered from the relation between observed gross occupation-sector transition rates and income differentials, with the contemporaneous differential instrumented as in Artuc-Chaudhuri-McLaren because workers adjust to shocks only with a lag, so next-period forecast errors are uncorrelated with the instruments.
units.instrument: The IV strategy of Artuç, Chaudhuri, and McLaren (2010); the specific instruments are not named in the main text (“I use exactly ACM’s estimator in each of specifications (2)-(4). Details are in onlin
units.source_of_variation: As in Artuç, Chaudhuri, and McLaren (2010): variation in observed gross transition rates across states and over time, with the contemporaneous wage differential instrumented because ACM assume workers adjust to contemporaneous shocks only with a lag.

units.summary: Switching costs and the dispersion of idiosyncratic cost shocks are identified from the dynamic choice structure: observationally identical workers who begin and end in the same occupation-sector state but take different intervening career arcs (finite dependence) differ only through the costs along those paths, given estimated skill prices over 1996-2008.
units.source_of_variation: Differences in observed transition rates across career arcs (o, o', o'') among workers with identical observed characteristics and unobserved type who begin and end in the same occupation-triple but make different intervening choices (finite dependence), combined with variation in estimated occupation-sector skill prices over 1996-2008. There is no external shock or reform: identification comes from the structure of the dynamic discrete choice model.

units.summary: The estimated labour-supply model together with the calibrated demand side is simulated with the 1996-2005 decline in foreign import prices and again with import prices frozen at base levels using the same idiosyncratic draws, so the difference traces the shock's effect on worker incomes, welfare and the share of income variance explained by occupation and sector groups.
units.source_of_variation: The simulated decline in foreign import prices from 1996 to 2005 fed through the calibrated general equilibrium model, compared with a counterfactual holding import prices fixed at base levels; the same idiosyncratic shocks are drawn in both simulations.

units.summary: Mean mobility costs for occupation-only, sector-only and joint moves are read off the cost matrix estimated in the model's second-stage nonlinear least squares and averaged over the empirical distribution of observed switchers.
units.source_of_variation: Estimated cost matrix C(o, o') from the second-stage nonlinear least squares on equation (17), averaged over the empirical distribution of switchers.

units.summary: A pseudo-EM first stage uses persistent within-worker income differences across occupation-sector cells to assign workers to a small number of unobserved comparative-advantage types, and workers who sit at different points of the income distribution in different occupations identify type-specific relative productivities, showing how omitting type biases the estimated return to occupational tenure.
units.source_of_variation: Unexplained persistence of income within worker-occupation-triple cells, which the pseudo-EM first stage uses to allocate workers to unobserved comparative-advantage types; movers who operate at different points of the income distribution in different occupations identify the relative productivities.

units.summary: The model-implied elasticity of exit from the current occupation-sector pair with respect to a transitory skill-price change is computed from the estimated 1/rho and the model's conditional choice probabilities, using no further data variation.
units.source_of_variation: The estimated value of 1/rho from column (1) of Table 5, combined with the model's conditional choice probabilities; no additional data variation is used.

units.summary: The exit response to a permanent one-percent fall in an occupation-sector pair's skill price is obtained by propagating the estimated 1/rho through the model's continuation values in a back-of-the-envelope calculation rather than a full simulation.
units.source_of_variation: The estimated value of 1/rho from column (1) of Table 5, propagated through the model's continuation values; a back-of-the-envelope calculation rather than a full simulation.

units.treatment: permanent skill-price decline, no human capital
units.summary: The same back-of-the-envelope exit response to a permanent one-percent skill-price decline is recomputed with the 1/rho estimates from specifications that ignore occupational human capital, so the implied mobility response reflects those alternative structural parameters.
units.source_of_variation: The estimates of 1/rho from the specifications of Table 5 that ignore occupational human capital (columns (4) and (5)), propagated through the same back-of-the-envelope calculation as the main specification.

units.summary: Descriptive OLS regressions compare standardized class 9 exam grades of children of intermarried parents with those of natives and second-generation immigrants, conditioning on observed child and parental characteristics and assuming no remaining family-level selection.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in parental nativity between students (and, in the fixed-effects columns, within schools or within extended families). No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used: 'the paper is mainly descriptive'.

units.summary: Adding school fixed effects, the grade gaps by parental nativity are identified only from students attending the same school, netting out school quality and neighbourhood composition.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in parental nativity between students (and, in the fixed-effects columns, within schools or within extended families). No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used: 'the paper is mainly descriptive'.

units.summary: Extended-family fixed effects compare children of intermarried parents with cousins whose parents married endogamously, so that unobserved values and upbringing shared within the extended family are held fixed.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in parental nativity between students (and, in the fixed-effects columns, within schools or within extended families). No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used: 'the paper is mainly descriptive'.

units.summary: The estimated distribution of marginal propensities to consume across deciles of interest-rate exposure, nominal position, income and consumption is plugged into Auclert's sufficient-statistic formulas to compute the model-implied aggregate consumption response to counterfactual income, price-level and interest-rate shocks.
units.source_of_variation: No external shock or reform. The sufficient statistics of Auclert (2019) are constructed from the cross-sectional distribution of the estimated transitory MPX across deciles of unhedged interest rate exposure, net nominal position, income and consumption, weighted by each decile's exposure and divided by aggregate consumption, with the exposure held outside the estimation sample allocated to seven bins so that aggregate exposure is zero. The underlying MPX estimates come from the covariance-restriction GMM described above.

units.summary: Because transitory shocks add a fixed amount of variance at the window's ends while permanent shocks accumulate linearly with the horizon, the way variances of multi-year income growth and their covariances with expenditure growth change as the horizon lengthens pins down the consumption responses to each income component, including by liquid-wealth quintile.
units.source_of_variation: No external shock or reform. Identification comes from covariance restrictions on panel data: the shape of the variance of N-year household income growth and of its covariance with N-year expenditure growth as the growth horizon N lengthens, because transitory shocks contribute a fixed amount of variance at the two ends of the window while permanent shocks accumulate linearly in N. Estimated on growth over three, four and five years in a continuous-time model that accounts for the time aggregation of annual data.

units.summary: The original Blundell–Pistaferri–Preston covariance restrictions are applied to the Danish administrative moments, with mean reversion of transitory shocks after one period and a random-walk consumption rule (with and without modelling time aggregation) identifying the transitory and permanent pass-through coefficients.
units.source_of_variation: The original Blundell, Pistaferri, and Preston (2008) covariance restrictions applied to moments obtained from the Danish administrative data: identification of the transitory response comes from the fact that a transitory shock in period t mean-reverts in period t+1, and consumption is assumed to follow a random walk. Time aggregation of the annual data is not modelled.

units.summary: Within-patient variation before versus after the nationwide April 2015 remuneration reform, with patient fixed effects and a post-reform time trend, identifies how the altered provider incentives changed the content and number of dental sessions.
units.source_of_variation: The 2015 reform: the collective agreement on adult dental care in force from 1 April 2015 (Regionernes Lønningsog Taksnævn, 2014) incorporating the Danish Health Authority's 2013 recall-interval guidelines, which made risk classification (green/yellow/red) and the IPT/FE codes the basis of remuneration. The reform applies nationwide and at once, so the variation exploited is purely before/after 1 April 2015.

units.summary: The same before/after reform contrast is estimated without patient fixed effects, instead conditioning on observed covariates (time, gender, age, municipality) assumed to absorb all confounding in session content.
units.source_of_variation: The 2015 reform: the collective agreement on adult dental care in force from 1 April 2015 (Regionernes Lønningsog Taksnævn, 2014) incorporating the Danish Health Authority's 2013 recall-interval guidelines, which made risk classification (green/yellow/red) and the IPT/FE codes the basis of remuneration. The reform applies nationwide and at once, so the variation exploited is purely before/after 1 April 2015.

units.summary: Refugees who obtained asylum after the first municipalities had filled their annual quota were allocated by the Immigration Service irrespective of their own preferences, so the labour-market conditions of the assigned municipality are as good as random conditional on the attributes the agency observed, and differences in later employment across assignees identify the effect of local labour demand
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of newly recognised refugees to municipalities under the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy in place from 1999: annual municipal refugee quotas set by the Danish Immigration Service, exploited for refugees who got asylum after the first 10 municipalities had filled their annual quota, when refugees' own settlement preferences can no longer be accommodated

units.summary: Using the same quota-driven placement of refugees, the characteristics of the municipality a refugee was assigned to are treated as exogenous conditional on observed attributes, and are related to the probability of leaving that municipality within four years to gauge subsequent location sorting.
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of refugees to municipalities under the Danish Spatial Dispersal Policy; the regression relates characteristics of the assigned municipality to the probability of later moving out of it

units.summary: As an observational benchmark, individual employment is regressed on the employment rate of the municipality the person currently lives in, conditioning only on covariates and assuming away self-selection into locations, so that the gap from the placement-based estimate reveals the direction of sorting bias.
units.source_of_variation: None beyond conditioning: the current local employment rate in the current municipality of residence, as in an observational data study, estimated to evaluate the direction of the bias from location sorting

units.summary: Patience (and risk aversion) elicited in an incentivized convex-time-budget experiment varies across individuals and is related, conditional on observed covariates, to register-measured wealth ranks and levels, with no exogenous variation in preferences claimed.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation across individuals in behaviourally revealed time discounting, elicited in an incentivized money-sooner-or-later (convex time budget) online experiment run in February 2015 with 3,620 invited Copenhagen-born residents. No exogenous variation in preferences is available: the authors state that it is impossible in practice to randomly assign type characteristics to people.

units.summary: Patience is proxied by a 1973 survey answer about preferred salary-profile timing given at ages 18-21 and linked to register wealth in 2001, so the measured preference is predetermined by nearly three decades relative to the wealth outcome it is compared across.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the answer given in 1973, at ages 18-21, to a Danish Longitudinal Survey of Youth question about the preferred timing of a salary profile, linked to register wealth 28 years later. No exogenous variation in preferences is claimed.

units.summary: Repeated panel observations of the same survey respondents let individual fixed effects absorb all time-invariant confounders, so only within-person changes in victimization between the two survey waves identify the change in reported insecurity.
units.source_of_variation: Ændring inden for det enkelte individ i selvrapporteret viktimisering mellem to på hinanden følgende undersøgelsesår (T1 og T2) blandt panelrespondenter i Dansk politis tryghedsundersøgelse 2014-2018; ingen ekstern eller politiskabt variation

units.summary: A GEE model compares insecurity between victimized and non-victimized respondents using both between- and within-person variation, assuming that conditioning on vulnerability markers and panel-set dummies removes remaining confounding.
units.source_of_variation: Ingen ekstern variation: GEE-modellen ('niveau- og ændringsanalyse') udnytter både variation på tværs af individer og variation inden for det enkelte individ over tid i selvrapporteret udsathed for kriminalitet blandt panelrespondenter i Dansk politis tryghedsundersøgelse 2014-2018, betinget på sårbarhedsmarkører og dummyvariable for de fire panelsæt

units.summary: Respondents are grouped by their victimization sequence across the two waves (newly victimized, no longer victimized, repeatedly victimized) and their change in insecurity is compared with that of respondents never victimized, which allows victims to start from a higher baseline level.
units.source_of_variation: Ændring i viktimiseringsstatus mellem T1 og T2 for grupperne 0-1, 1-0 og 1-1 sammenlignet med udviklingen for referencegruppen 0-0 (ikke-viktimiseret i begge år); DID-analyserne er kørt med de samme variable som model I-III i tabel 1

units.summary: Among first-time inmates held in the same facility-by-prior-offense cell, the length of time each one happens to overlap in prison with fellow inmates convicted of a given offense type varies quasi-randomly with the timing of entry and release, so offense-specific recidivism can be compared across inmates with more or less exposure to peers with that criminal history.
units.source_of_variation: random variation in the duration of overlap in incarceration between a first-time inmate and each fellow inmate with a criminal history of offense h, within facility-by-prior-offense cells (facility, quarter-of-release and facility-by-prior-offense fixed effects included)

atlas.from_label: Exposure to peers in other crime types

units.summary: The same within-facility-by-prior-offense peer exposure measures are related to recidivism predicted from pre-determined individual and municipality characteristics, so any systematic gap would reveal selection into peer composition rather than a causal peer effect.
units.source_of_variation: variation in peer composition within facility-by-prior-offense cells

units.summary: Because national salt iodization raised iodine intake most where naturally occurring iodine in drinking water was lowest, GPA of post-reform cohorts is compared with pre-reform cohorts across municipalities differing in geologically determined pre-reform iodine concentration, with the reform date giving the time dimension and water iodine the dose.
units.source_of_variation: Introduction of iodized salt in Denmark - a voluntary program from June 1998 and a mandatory program phased in between July 2000 and April 2001 - interacted with pre-existing, geologically determined cross-municipality variation in the iodine concentration of drinking water

units.summary: The municipality-level change in average GPA before versus after iodization is fitted as a third-order polynomial in the pre-reform degree of iodine deficiency and extrapolated past the Danish range to predict the GPA gain from correcting moderate and severe deficiency.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-municipality variation in the pre-reform degree of iodine deficiency, related to the municipality-level change in average standardized GPA between 1988-1998 and 2002-2006, fitted with a third-order polynomial and extrapolated beyond the Danish range

units.summary: The 1999 reform cut the capital-pension deduction only for top-bracket earners, so workplaces with a larger share of employees above the top tax threshold were mechanically more exposed, and the change in the exposure gradient of employer contribution rates after the reform relative to pre-reform years identifies the effect.
units.source_of_variation: The 1999 Danish tax reform, which reduced the average deduction for contributions to capital pension accounts from 59 to 45 cents per DKr for individuals in the top labor income tax bracket while leaving the deduction for lower-bracket workers and for annuity contributions unchanged; workplaces differ in the share of employees above the top tax threshold (continuous treatment intensity) and the gradient is compared across years with 1998 omitted

atlas.from_label: reform decreasing the subsidy to contributions to capital pension accounts

units.summary: An appendix check compares labor income of workers more versus less exposed to the 1999 deduction cut around the reform to see whether employers offset the reform through wages, but the published article does not report the specification, so the identification cannot be read off the paper.
units.source_of_variation: The 1999 reform; the specification behind this statement is in online Appendix C, which is not included in the published article, so the design cannot be read off the paper

units.summary: Married couples whose prereform wealth placed them in brackets hit hard by the 1989 wealth tax cut are compared over time with couples in brackets whose wealth tax burden changed little, with prereform-based group status used to instrument contemporaneous status so that endogenous bracket movement after the reform does not drive the estimates.
units.instrument: Year_{j=t} · Treat_i^pre — year dummies interacted with prereform (1982–88) treatment status, instrumenting the concurrent Year_{j=t} · Treat_it
units.source_of_variation: The 1989 Danish wealth tax reform: the marginal wealth tax rate was cut from 2.2% to 1% between 1989 and 1991 and the exemption threshold for married couples was doubled relative to singles between 1989 and 1992.

units.summary: A life cycle savings model with warm-glow utility of residual wealth is calibrated to the reform's medium-run quasi-experimental effects and the observed age profile of top wealth, then simulated forward to recover the long-run mechanical and behavioral response of wealth to a permanent wealth tax cut.
units.source_of_variation: The quasi-experimental TOT effects of the 1989 Danish wealth tax reform for 1989–96, combined with the empirical life cycle profile of taxable wealth at the top of the distribution, used to calibrate a life cycle model with utility of residual wealth and to simulate it forward.

units.summary: The 1989 rate cut and the doubling of the married-couple exemption threshold changed wealth tax burdens by differing amounts across prereform wealth brackets, so comparing wealth paths of more- and less-exposed couples before and after the reform yields intention-to-treat effects and, scaled by the change in the net-of-tax rate, the elasticity of taxable wealth.
units.source_of_variation: The 1989 Danish wealth tax reform: the marginal wealth tax rate was cut from 2.2% to 1% between 1989 and 1991 and the exemption threshold for married couples was doubled relative to singles between 1989 and 1992.

atlas.from_label: Marginal tax rate on labor income

units.summary: Parents of children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes are compared before and after diagnosis with matched control parents assigned a pseudo-onset date, treating the unpredictable, lifestyle-unrelated onset as a health shock unrelated to parental labor market paths.
units.source_of_variation: The onset of type 1 diabetes in a child, which the authors argue is unpredictable, of unknown cause, unrelated to lifestyle and of low inheritability, compared against matched control children's pseudo-onset

units.summary: The same before-after comparison of diagnosed versus matched control families is interacted with maternal and child characteristics, so the unpredictable timing of the child's diabetes onset identifies how the parental labor supply response differs across subgroups.
units.source_of_variation: The onset of type 1 diabetes in a child, interacted with a maternal or child sub-group indicator

units.summary: Parental labor market outcomes are traced year by year around the child's diabetes diagnosis relative to matched control children's pseudo-onset, so the dynamic path after event time zero (with flat pre-event differences) identifies the shock's effect.
units.source_of_variation: The onset of type 1 diabetes in a child at event time t = 0, against matched control children's pseudo-onset

units.summary: Sisters from the same family are compared on adult earnings and schooling where the later-childbearing sister's first birth was pushed past the age cutoff by a miscarriage, so family background is differenced out and the remaining timing difference comes from the health event.
units.source_of_variation: Combination of the two strategies: within-family (sister) variation in the age at first childbirth where the non-early childbearing sister's first birth was delayed by a miscarriage before age 25 - miscarriage supplies the variation in timing and the sister fixed effect absorbs family background.; sample restricted to the lower socioeconomic-background half: women whose mother's education length is at or below the overall sample median of 8 years (women whose mothers have exactly the median length are included in the lower group)

units.summary: The same sister fixed-effect comparison combined with miscarriage-induced delay is run on small-sibship samples and alternative age cutoffs, identifying the effect from within-family timing differences generated by the miscarriage.
units.source_of_variation: Combination of the two strategies: within-family (sister) variation in the age at first childbirth where the non-early childbearing sister's first birth was delayed by a miscarriage before age 25 - miscarriage supplies the variation in timing and the sister fixed effect absorbs family background.; sister samples restricted to families with no more than three sisters; the table note says the sample consists of families with only one early and one non-early childbearing sister

units.summary: Early childbearers are compared cross-sectionally with women who were also pregnant young but miscarried, so the comparison group's delayed first birth reflects a health shock rather than different life plans.
units.source_of_variation: Miscarriages treated as exogenous variation in the timing of childbearing: the comparison group consists of women who were also pregnant before turning 25 but whose first childbirth was delayed by a miscarriage (and who did not have an induced abortion). Estimated by cross-sectional OLS, not by instrumental variables.; sample restricted to the lower socioeconomic-background half: women whose mother's education length is at or below the overall sample median of 8 years (women whose mothers have exactly the median length are included in the lower group)

units.summary: Within families containing both an early and a later childbearing sister, the sister fixed effect absorbs shared family background and the remaining difference in age at first birth identifies the effect on earnings and schooling.
units.source_of_variation: Within-family (sister) variation in the age at first childbirth: families in which at least one sister gave birth before turning 25 and at least one did not. No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used.; sample restricted to the lower socioeconomic-background half: women whose mother's education length is at or below the overall sample median of 8 years (women whose mothers have exactly the median length are included in the lower group)

units.summary: For labour-supply and wage outcomes the paper reports its two single-strategy designs side by side, the identification in this unit resting on comparing early childbearers with observationally similar women whose first birth a miscarriage delayed.
units.source_of_variation: A statement covering both of the paper's single-strategy designs at once: the sister fixed-effect estimator on sample 1 and the cross-sectional OLS using miscarriages as exogenous variation on sample 2.

units.summary: Long differencing firm-level data between 2006 and 2010 sweeps out time-invariant firm heterogeneity, so the observed within-firm changes in work-organization factors, technological change and off-shoring status identify their effect on changes in occupational wage cost shares, conditional on sales, local relative wages and crisis controls.
units.source_of_variation: Within-firm change between 2006 and 2010 in the quasi-fixed factors of the translog cost function - work organization (the DI and INV factors), an indicator of technological change in production, and the start or cessation of off-shoring - with firm-specific unobserved heterogeneity removed by long differencing. There is no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument: the variation is the observed change in firms' own practices.

units.summary: Short-run changes in the market value of a woman's first home, purged of municipality-by-year and purchase-age-by-purchase-year fixed effects, identify how housing wealth shocks affect her fertility and her newborn's health.
units.source_of_variation: Short-run (once-lagged one-year) variation in the estimated market value of the first home a woman purchased, net of municipality-by-year and age-of-purchase-by-year-of-purchase fixed effects; Danish housing market 1993-2006, including the boom of the early- to mid-2000s

units.summary: Comparing expenditure of observationally similar two-adult households that differ in the number of children under two, conditioning on older children, income, both adults' age and education, region and time, gives the consumption cost of an infant.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the number of children under age two across observationally similar two-adult households in the 2015-2018 US Consumer Expenditure Surveys

units.summary: The same within-municipality-year home price variation is applied to women who own no home, so any estimated fertility response would signal local shocks rather than housing wealth.
units.source_of_variation: Municipality-level one-year home price changes experienced by women who are not home owners and therefore have no housing wealth exposure (placebo test for local shocks)

units.summary: Baseline self-reported bullying exposure is compared across workers in a prospective register-linked cohort, with Cox-model adjustment for sex, age, living status, socio-economic status and prior psychiatric morbidity assumed to remove confounding.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used: this is an observational prospective cohort. The contrast is between-person differences in self-reported exposure to workplace bullying at baseline, with register-based adjustment for sex, age, living status, socio-economic status and previous history of psychiatric morbidity, and with robust variance clustered on survey wave.

units.summary: Variance components of permanent log earnings are identified from the covariance structure of life-cycle earnings: sibling covariances net of community covariances give family effects, while the gap in sibling covariances between siblings who do and do not share the age-15 community (created by family moves between ages 11 and 15) gives community effects.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous shock or reform: the paper identifies variance components from the covariance structure of life-cycle earnings across persons. Family effects come from sibling covariances net of community covariances; community effects come from the difference in sibling covariances between siblings who do and do not share the youth community at age 15 (generated by family mobility between ages 11 and 15); sorting is identified from community-peer covariances.

units.summary: Family and community variance components of the latent propensity to receive unemployment benefits are recovered from the covariance structure of Tobit errors across ages, across siblings who do and do not share the youth community, and across community peers.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous shock or reform: variance components of the latent unemployment propensity are identified from the covariance structure of Tobit errors across time, siblings (sharing and not sharing the community) and community peers.

units.summary: Family, school-community and sorting components of years of education are identified by matching cohort-specific empirical moments—sibling covariances for siblings who do and do not share the school, schoolmate covariances and individual variances—to a time-invariant variance-components model.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous shock or reform: family, school-community and sorting components of years of education are identified from sibling covariances (siblings who do and do not share the school), schoolmate covariances and individual variances, using 68 cohort-specific empirical moments.

units.summary: Among first-born daughters whose parents had a second child, the second child's sex is effectively randomly assigned, so comparing women with a younger brother to women with a younger sister identifies the causal effect of sibling sex on the gender-typicality of their occupation and partner choice.
units.source_of_variation: Random assignment of the sex of the second-born child in families whose first-born child is a daughter, conditional on the parents having a second child: parents do not know the sex of an unborn child when they decide to have another child

units.summary: Using the same as-good-as-random sex of the second-born child, the paper traces earnings and accumulated work experience by age for first-born daughters with a brother versus a sister, showing when over the life cycle the sibling-sex effect emerges.
units.source_of_variation: Random assignment of the sex of the second-born child in families whose first-born child is a daughter, conditional on the parents having a second child: parents do not know the sex of an unborn child when they decide to have another child

units.summary: Because unanticipated closures of Danish private-sector firms push some workers into unemployment for reasons unrelated to their fertility plans, a monthly closure dummy instruments individual unemployment in hazard models of first and second conceptions.
units.instrument: Firm closure (a monthly dummy for the closure of the private-sector firm employing the individual)
units.source_of_variation: Unexpected closures of private-sector Danish firms with more than four employees, 1982-2006, used as an exogenous source of individual unemployment; 11,778 of the 74,556 individuals in the first sample (15.8 percent) and 2992 of the 41,432 in the second sample (7.2 percent) experienced at least one closure.

units.summary: Because the rule sends children to school in the year they turn seven, being born just after January 1 discontinuously raises the probability of being young for grade, and this jump is used to instrument relative age for grade in outcomes like abortion, alcohol poisoning and contraception.
units.instrument: cutoff: dummy equal to one if the woman is born in January or February (born January 1 or later)
units.source_of_variation: The administrative rule that children should start school in the calendar year they turn seven, which creates a discontinuous jump in relative age for grade for children born around January 1; women born November-February 1981/82-1991/92
