units.summary: The woman's own birth-date position relative to January 1 and the rule-implied average expected school starting age of her grade-8 peers serve as two instruments, separating the effect of her own relative age for grade from that of her classmates' average age.
units.instrument: born January 1 or later (for young-for-grade) and the grade-8 peers' average expected school starting age (for peers' average age)
units.source_of_variation: The school starting age rule, used both for the woman's own relative age for grade (instrument: born January 1 or later) and for her grade-8 peers' average age (instrument: the peers' average expected age according to the school starting age rule, ESSA = 7.6-(birthmonth-1)/12)

units.summary: Comparing women born in the two months just before and just after New Year isolates the discontinuous increase in being young for grade caused purely by falling on the later side of the school-entry birth-date rule.
units.source_of_variation: The administrative rule that children should start school in the calendar year they turn seven, which creates a discontinuous jump in relative age for grade at January 1; women born November-February, +/- two months around New Year

units.summary: The same January 1 discontinuity instruments relative age for grade, with births in the days immediately around New Year dropped so that scheduled deliveries cannot drive the jump.
units.instrument: cutoff: dummy equal to one if the woman is born in January or February
units.source_of_variation: The administrative school starting age rule creating a discontinuous jump in relative age for grade at January 1, with the days immediately around New Year excluded because planned C-sections are not performed on holidays

units.summary: The intention-to-treat discontinuity at the January 1 birth-date rule shows how much being born on the later side shifts a woman's relative age for grade, assuming birth timing is not manipulated around the cutoff.
units.source_of_variation: The administrative school starting age rule creating a discontinuous jump in relative age for grade at January 1

units.summary: Comparing the SHARE survey report, the 1970 census self-report and post-1970 institutional qualification records, with institutional records treated as error-free for the 25% subsample and the nonclassical error component assumed common to survey and census, yields moment restrictions that pin down the true and error variances of schooling in both subsamples.
units.source_of_variation: A three-way comparison of the SHARE survey report, the 1970 census self-report and post-1970 third-party institutional reports of qualifications: the sample splits into one part whose validation data are assumed error-free (institutional reports, 25%) and one whose validation data are of the same first-party nature as the survey (census, 75%), an external validation study within an internal validation study

units.summary: The register income measure serves as an independent second measurement of survey-reported income, and third-party register variables (gender and log assets) assumed unrelated to survey response error act as instruments, so the instrumented survey–register relation identifies the classical and nonclassical error components without assuming the register is error-free.
units.instrument: Gender and the logarithm of assets at the end of 2003, both third-party reported in the Danish registers
units.source_of_variation: Two independent measures of the same 2003 gross income for the same individual -- the SHARE survey self-report and the third-party-reported Danish tax register -- combined with third-party register instruments (gender and the logarithm of assets at the end of 2003) that are correlated with income but assumed independent of first-party survey response error

units.summary: Taking the Danish tax register (and administrative schooling record) as the true value and assuming survey–register linkage is exact, the joint distribution of the survey report and the validation measure identifies the variance of the true quantity and of classical and nonclassical survey error as a benchmark later relaxed.
units.source_of_variation: Comparison of the SHARE survey self-report of 2003 gross income with the Danish tax register measure of the same quantity, under the benchmark assumption that the register measure is the true value

atlas.to_label: IV estimates of the returns to schooling

units.summary: Covariance restrictions on time-aggregated income and imputed-expenditure growth in Danish register panels separate permanent from transitory idiosyncratic income shocks and pin down the consumption-response parameters, which are then combined with register measures of households' unhedged interest exposure, net nominal positions and income to compute Auclert's sufficient statistics for the aggreg
units.source_of_variation: idiosyncratic 'typical' permanent and transitory income shocks of Danish households, identified from covariance restrictions on time-aggregated income and imputed-expenditure growth, combined with register measures of households' URE, NNP and income positions in Auclert's (2019) decomposition

units.summary: The marginal-propensity schedule estimated over Danish liquid wealth is interpolated onto US households' balance-sheet and income positions in the 2016 Survey of Consumer Finances, so that the estimated structural parameters deliver the model-implied sufficient statistics for the aggregate-income, earnings-heterogeneity and Fisher channels in the US distribution.
units.source_of_variation: household balance-sheet positions (URE, NNP, income, liquid wealth) in the 2016 Survey of Consumer Finances, combined with MPXs interpolated from the Danish liquid-wealth MPX schedule, in Auclert's (2019) decomposition

units.summary: Children aged 45-50 whose last living parent dies in 2010 are compared with children whose parent remains alive, differencing each child's wealth between 2008 and 2011 (with the control group reweighted on parental wealth rank), so the inheritance-induced change in the child wealth distribution is identified by the timing of the parent's death.
units.source_of_variation: Timing of death of the last living biological parent: parents who die in 2010 versus parents still alive, with wealth differenced between 2008 and 2011

units.summary: The treatment-control difference in average child wealth is traced year by year around the 2010 death of the last living parent, so flat pre-death differences and the jump at death identify the bequest effect from the event's timing.
units.source_of_variation: Timing of death of the last living biological parent: parents who die in 2010 versus parents still alive, with wealth differenced between 2008 and 2011

units.summary: The dated onset of a first long unemployment spell among previously stably employed individuals, compared with a reweighted continuously employed control group and individual fixed effects, traces how the shock moves the affected person's and their parents' incomes.
units.source_of_variation: the timing of a first unemployment spell of at least three months in 2007, 2008 or 2009 among individuals with five clean preceding years, relative to an otherwise similar control group

units.summary: Cross-sectional differences in survey-elicited risk willingness, patience and impulsivity, conditional on the other traits and a covariate set, are related to default of the respondent and of the parent generation.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional variation in self-assessed behavioural characteristics across survey respondents, holding the other two behavioural measures and the Figure 5 covariate set fixed

units.summary: The parents' decile of their financial asset-to-disposable-income ratio measured a decade and a half earlier instruments current parental default, isolating the persistent latent financial-behaviour component transmitted to the child's default.
units.instrument: within-parental-cohort decile of the ratio of average financial assets to average disposable income for the parents across the years 1987–96
units.source_of_variation: variation in parental default in 2011 predicted by the within-cohort decile of the parents' average financial asset-to-disposable-income ratio over 1987–96

units.summary: Residual differences in parental default, after conditioning on income, education, employment, region, cohort and bank fixed effects, identify the part of the intergenerational default correlation not explained by those observed channels.
units.source_of_variation: residual variation in parental default status in 2011 after conditioning on a large set of income, education, employment, region, cohort and bank dummies

units.summary: Absorbing a time-invariant parent–child specific component from the panel of defaults over 2004–11 leaves only within-pair co-movement in default across years as the source of variation.
units.source_of_variation: within parent–child pair variation in default over 2004–11, after absorbing a fixed intergenerational component

units.summary: The dated onset of an unanticipated parental unemployment spell is used to test whether the other generation's financial wealth, loan counts and debt levels move, as evidence on resource pooling.
units.source_of_variation: the timing of parental unemployment shocks in 2007, 2008 or 2009

units.summary: Parents are ranked by their financial asset-to-disposable-income ratio measured many years before the outcome, and this predetermined ranking is related to their later default probability.
units.instrument: within-parental-cohort decile of the ratio of average financial assets to average disposable income for the parents across the years 1987–96
units.source_of_variation: variation across parents in the historical (1987–96) ratio of financial assets to disposable income

units.summary: A search model of listing and selling is fitted to cross-sectional variation in potential nominal gains and home equity, the listing-premium and sale-probability profiles and cross-municipality demand concavity, so listing behaviour not explained by demand curvature pins down loss aversion around the nominal purchase price.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation across 214,103 Danish listings in potential gains Ĝ = ln P̂ − ln R and potential home equity Ĥ = ln P̂ − ln M, the distribution of realized gains around zero, the listing propensity of the housing stock across potential gains, and cross-municipality variation in the concavity of demand

atlas.from_label: Nominal gain on the home relative to its purchase price

units.summary: The estimated model's parameters are used to simulate how year-to-year municipality price changes map into transaction volumes, and switching reference dependence on and off decomposes the model-implied price-volume correlation.
units.source_of_variation: Year-to-year variation in average hedonic price levels and transaction counts across the 98 Danish municipalities, 2009-2016

units.summary: Comparing the distribution of realized nominal gains with the counterfactual distribution of potential gains among sales shows excess mass exactly at a zero gain and missing mass just below, revealing sellers' reluctance to sell below the nominal purchase price.
units.source_of_variation: Shift of mass in the distribution of realized nominal gains relative to the counterfactual distribution of potential gains among realized sales, in 1 percentage point bins

units.summary: The share of apartments and near-identical row houses in a municipality is used as an instrument for how concave local housing demand is, so that the part of the cross-municipality listing-premium profile in the loss domain attributable to demand curvature can be separated from seller loss aversion.
units.instrument: Homogeneity of the local housing stock (share of apartments and 'cookie cutter' row houses) in the municipality
units.source_of_variation: Cross-municipality variation in demand concavity instrumented by the homogeneity of the local housing stock (share of apartments and 'cookie cutter' row houses)

units.summary: An on-the-job search model is fitted to the cross-sectional distribution of workplace stayer counts across Danish private-sector workplaces, using the exogenous nonlinear effective marginal tax schedule mapped onto workplace wage levels to pin down the search, destruction and mobility-cost parameters, which are then used to simulate how taxation reallocates labor and affects non-employment and agg
units.source_of_variation: No reform or experiment: the structural parameters are identified from cross-sectional variation across 126,400 Danish private-sector workplaces in 2005 in the number of stayers x_h out of n_h employees (the 2005-to-2006 separation rate), combined with the exogenous effective marginal tax schedule of the Danish 2006 tax system (Kleven and Kreiner, 2006) mapped onto workplace average hourly wage rates, and with the offered wage distribution P estimated from workers hired from non-employment. The authors state the analysis 'exploits only cross-sectional variation across individuals for identific

units.summary: Twin births, treated as an unanticipated biological addition to completed fertility, are used as re-centred parity-specific instruments for family size, so the education effect is identified from fertility variation unrelated to the family's unobserved effect.
units.instrument: twin birth at the last birth (z_j = z-tilde^{N_j-1}_j)
units.source_of_variation: twin births as an exogenous, unanticipated and undiversifiable addition to completed family size (re-centred twin-birth-at-parity-k indicators z^k_j = (z-tilde^k_j - E[z-tilde^k_j | N_j >= k]) I(N_j >= k), k = 3, ..., N+ - 1, equation (15)); within-family variation across siblings for the birth order profile

units.summary: Comparing siblings of different birth order within the same family absorbs all time-invariant family characteristics, so the birth-order profile of education is identified from within-family differences alone.
units.source_of_variation: within-family variation in educational attainment across siblings of different birth order

units.summary: Cross-family differences in completed family size and birth order are regressed on education with observed family controls, assuming no remaining correlation with unobserved family determinants.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional variation in completed family size and birth order across Danish families, with no exogenous variation claimed

units.summary: Identification comes from the dated phase-out of MFA quotas tied to China's WTO accession, comparing imports of the same goods from China (or of formerly quota-constrained goods, and firms that produced such goods pre-accession) with imports from unaffected countries and non-quota goods before and after 2002 and 2005.
units.source_of_variation: Abolishment of the Multi-fibre Arrangement (MFA) quotas on Chinese textile and clothing goods following China's accession to the WTO (Phases I-III removed January 2002, Phase IV January 2005); across-firm variation comes from whether a Danish T&C firm produced MFA quota goods in 1999, before the accession.

units.summary: Unemployment exit hazards are compared across spells that differ only in why the previous workplace shed the worker (closure, severe or moderate downsizing, expansion, no change), conditioning on detailed demographic, human-capital, job and location controls so that the displacement reason acts as an ability signal independent of unobserved worker quality.
units.source_of_variation: Variation across unemployment spells in the reason for displacement from the previous workplace — workplace closure, severe downsizing (50%–99% or 10%–50% workforce reduction), leaving an expanding workplace, or a workplace with no change in employment (±10%) — for men aged 18–59 entering unemployment in Denmark 1994–1999. The authors argue company closures are exogenous in the sense of not being caused by their own workforce, so no low-ability inference can be drawn from closure-induced displacement.

atlas.from_label: proportion of employees dismissed from the workplace

units.summary: Because mothers cannot finely control birth weight, newborns just below the 1,500 gram guideline threshold receive extra early-life medical treatment while otherwise comparable newborns just above do not, so comparing mortality and health outcomes of focal children and their siblings across the cutoff (local linear fit, 200g triangular-kernel bandwidth) identifies the treatment's own and spillover
units.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

units.summary: School fixed effects, cohort dummies and school-specific linear trends leave only year-to-year fluctuations in a school's grade-9 size, which are compared with the later educational and labour-market outcomes of successive cohorts from the same school.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in school size within the same school over the grade 9 cohorts 1986-2004, net of school-specific linear trends

units.summary: Demographic fluctuations in the number of school-aged children living in a school's catchment area shift its enrolment and, under the assumption that catchment population affects students only through school size, instrument the effect of school size on outcomes.
units.instrument: Catchment area size (CAS)/100: the number of children in the catchment area aged 7-16 years at the end of the year, divided by 100
units.source_of_variation: Natural population variation in the residential catchment area (number of children aged 7-16 in the catchment area), combined with school fixed effects

units.summary: Within-school, within-cohort differences in individual and parental background characteristics are related to outcomes conditional on school and cohort fixed effects, yielding partial correlations rather than causal effects.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the control variables within schools

units.summary: Siblings who attended the same school in different grade-9 cohorts faced different school sizes, so family fixed effects strip out shared family background and the remaining within-family size differences identify the effect.
units.source_of_variation: Differences in school size between siblings who attended the same school in different grade 9 cohorts

units.summary: When a municipality politically decides to open or close a school, neighbouring schools' sizes jump; these reorganization-driven jumps are used as exogenous shocks instrumenting school size.
units.instrument: School openings and closings (SOC)/100: the change in school size from one year to the next if a school opens (closes) in the municipality of the school, zero otherwise, divided by 100
units.source_of_variation: School openings and closings in the municipality of the school during 1986-2004, used as shocks to school size

units.summary: The first stage shows that natural variation in the number of children in a school's catchment area strongly predicts the school's size, establishing instrument relevance.
units.instrument: Instrument (CAS)/100
units.source_of_variation: Natural population variation in the residential catchment area

units.summary: The first stage shows that openings and closings of other schools in the municipality shift a school's size, establishing relevance of the reorganization instrument.
units.instrument: Instrument (SOC - openings)/100
units.source_of_variation: School openings and closings in the municipality of the school

units.summary: Raw cross-school and over-time differences in school size are related to outcomes conditional on cohort dummies and a rich set of individual, parental and catchment-area controls, assuming no remaining unobserved sorting into school sizes.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional and over-time variation in school size across Danish public schools 1986-2004, conditional on a wide set of individual, parental and catchment area controls

units.summary: Retailers that begin importing consumer goods from outside the EU15 are compared with non-importing retailers matched on their estimated propensity to start importing, so that conditional on pre-determined firm characteristics the import start is treated as if randomly assigned.
units.source_of_variation: Danish retailers that start importing consumer goods from non-EU15 markets in year t (no imports in t-1 and t-2), compared with non-importing retailers matched on the estimated propensity to start importing

units.summary: Concentration of local retail markets is related to changes in sector-level direct imports from outside the EU15 within region-by-sector markets over time, with the rise in imports taken as a proxy for falling trade costs and the correlation read as suggestive rather than causal.
units.source_of_variation: within local retail market (region x sector) variation in sector-level direct consumer goods imports from outside the EU15, 1999-2008

units.summary: Import premia are estimated from differences in import status across retailers within sector-year cells and, with firm fixed effects, from firms that switch into or out of direct importing, assuming such switches are unrelated to time-varying unobserved firm determinants of performance.
units.source_of_variation: cross-firm (and, with firm fixed effects, within-firm) variation in direct import status of Danish retailers, 1999-2008; the authors assume the observed increase in import activity is at least in part driven by a trade cost reduction

units.summary: Assuming male and female labor are perfect substitutes up to a scalar and that female efficiency units can be predicted from a male-only earnings regression, variation across firms and years within industry in the gender composition of the workforce identifies female labor's marginal product in a value-added production function, which is then compared with the female wage bill.
units.source_of_variation: Variation across firms and years, within 2-digit industry, in the gender composition of the workforce measured in efficiency units, related to firm value added. Gender is not randomly assigned; the author states that the gender productivity gap and the gender pay gap are fundamentally descriptive statistics.

units.summary: The same production function is estimated with labor disaggregated into age bins crossed with gender/parenthood groups (including women with high predicted future fertility), so cross-firm variation in group composition yields each group's marginal product, which is differenced against group wage regressions to compare pay and productivity gaps relative to same-age men.
units.source_of_variation: Variation across firms in the composition of the workforce by group and age, combined with wage regressions for the same groups.

units.summary: Comparing women of the same age and calendar year who have their first child at different times, event-time coefficients around the first birth (with individual, age and year fixed effects) trace how motherhood shifts the pay premium of the firm a woman works for and her presence in the private sector.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the timing of the first birth across women who are the same age in the same calendar year, following Kleven, Landais, and Soegaard (2019).

units.summary: Workers moving between firms in the connected set identify AKM firm fixed effects under exogenous mobility, and the average firm effect is then compared by gender to measure sorting of women into lower-premium firms.
units.source_of_variation: Movements of workers between firms in the connected set of private-sector firms.

units.summary: Danish industries' 1999-2009 rise in Chinese import penetration is instrumented by the same industries' Chinese import growth in eight other high-income countries (plus a transport-cost measure), so only the China-supply-driven component of exposure, varying within two-digit industries, is used to estimate effects on workers' cumulative earnings, employment and hours, including by gender and age.
units.instrument: HIP^CH_j = (OM^CH_{j,2009} − OM^CH_{j,1999}) / C_{j,1996}, the change in Chinese imports in eight high-income countries (Australia, Finland, Germany, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland a
units.source_of_variation: Variation across six-digit industries in the 1999–2009 change in Chinese import penetration in Denmark (imports from China over domestic absorption), following the sudden expansion of Chinese production capabilities around its WTO accession, using variation within two-digit industries.

units.summary: Workers whose 1999 firm produced goods whose Chinese export quotas were lifted when the Multi-fibre Arrangement ended are compared before and after with otherwise similar textile workers whose goods kept quotas, with the exposure dated well before China's WTO entry and further interacted with gender and age.
units.source_of_variation: The removal of Multi-fibre Arrangement (MFA) quotas on China's textile and clothing exports to the European Union following China's entry into the WTO in December 2001: China benefited from Phases I–III in 2002 and from Phase IV in 2005, and a worker is exposed if his or her 1999 firm had domestic production of an eight-digit CN good whose Chinese quota was lifted. Neither Denmark nor China negotiated the creation or removal of the quotas.

atlas.to_label: Gender gap in earnings from children

units.summary: Year-by-year interactions of quota-removal exposure (and its interaction with being female) trace outcomes of exposed versus unexposed 1999 textile workers around the phased lifting of Chinese quotas, with pre-2002 years showing no divergence and post-reform years identifying the dynamic effect.
units.source_of_variation: The removal of Multi-fibre Arrangement (MFA) quotas on China's textile and clothing exports to the European Union following China's entry into the WTO in December 2001: China benefited from Phases I–III in 2002 and from Phase IV in 2005, and a worker is exposed if his or her 1999 firm had domestic production of an eight-digit CN good whose Chinese quota was lifted. Neither Denmark nor China negotiated the creation or removal of the quotas.

units.summary: Respondents were randomly assigned to blocks of EQ-5D-5L health states valued by cTTO and DCE, and a censored hybrid additive main-effects model fitted to these experimentally varied states recovers the utility decrement of each dimension level.
units.source_of_variation: Experimental variation in the EQ-5D-5L health states respondents were asked to value: a standardized blocked EQ-VT design in which 86 health states were valued in blocks of ten by cTTO (and 196 pairs in 28 blocks of seven by DCE), with respondents randomly assigned to a block and randomised order of states.

units.summary: The utility decrements estimated in the hybrid model are summed additively across the five level-5 dimensions to predict the value of state 55555, a state never directly valued, assuming the fitted parameters extrapolate to all 3125 states.
units.source_of_variation: The hybrid model's estimated utility decrements, applied additively to the dimension levels of state 55555.

units.summary: Because the reminder-letter policy started on a fixed date, children whose second birthday fell just after that date were sent a letter while otherwise identical children with birthdays just before were not, so comparing vaccination outcomes across this unmanipulable birth-date cutoff identifies the letter's effect.
units.source_of_variation: The nationwide introduction of the Danish vaccination reminder letter policy on 15 May 2014: parents of a child registered as lacking at least one scheduled vaccination at age 2 receive a reminder letter if, and only if, the child's second-year birthday falls on or after that date.

units.summary: Short-run changes in the market value of a woman's (or her partner's) first home, compared across otherwise similar buyers within municipality-year and purchase-age-by-purchase-year cells, are treated as conditionally unrelated to unobserved determinants of fertility and infant health.
units.source_of_variation: Short-run (one-year) variation in the estimated market value of the first home the woman or her partner purchased, used within municipality-by-year and age-of-purchase-by-year-of-purchase cells; the period spans the Danish housing boom of the early- to mid-2000s. The paper describes the design as the reduced form of using first-home price changes as an instrument for the price changes actually experienced.

units.summary: Expenditure is compared across observationally similar two-adult US households that do and do not have a child under two, conditioning on income, demographics and other covariates, to read off the consumption response to a birth.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the presence of children under age two across observationally similar two-adult US households in the 2015-2018 CEX.

units.summary: Identification comes from within-cell variation in first-home values, netting out municipality-by-year and age-of-purchase-by-year-of-purchase fixed effects so that only idiosyncratic timing and size of price changes drives the comparison.
units.source_of_variation: Short-run (one-year) variation in the estimated market value of the first home the woman or her partner purchased, used within municipality-by-year and age-of-purchase-by-year-of-purchase cells; the period spans the Danish housing boom of the early- to mid-2000s. The paper describes the design as the reduced form of using first-home price changes as an instrument for the price changes actually experienced.

units.summary: Renters face the same local home price movements but gain no housing wealth, so their conditional fertility response to municipality-level price changes gauges whether unobserved local shocks, rather than wealth, drive the main estimates.
units.source_of_variation: Municipality-level one-year home price changes experienced by renters, who are exposed to the same local shocks but to no housing wealth effect.

units.summary: Danish households with and without a child under two are compared on consumption imputed from income and year-to-year wealth changes, conditional on observables, to benchmark the Danish consumption response against the US estimate.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the presence of a child under age two across Danish households, with consumption imputed from income and wealth flows.

units.summary: Lagged, beginning-of-year stocks of broad R&D, organizational and ICT capital are related to firm TFP within firms, with firm and year fixed effects absorbing persistent firm heterogeneity and common shocks so that only within-firm changes in intangible stocks drive the estimated elasticities.
units.source_of_variation: within-firm variation over 2000-2013 in beginning-of-year stocks of broad R&D, organizational and ICT assets built from occupational labour costs

units.summary: Input elasticities are identified from across-firm and over-time variation in capital, labour and intangible stocks in a panel production function where unobserved technical efficiency is controlled for by inverting the monotone investment policy (Olley-Pakes) and modelled as a Markov process.
units.source_of_variation: variation in capital, labour, intangible stocks and investment across firms and years in an unbalanced panel of Finnish firms 2000-2013; unobserved productivity proxied by investment following Olley-Pakes

units.summary: Within education-by-institution cells, the average entering-cohort high school GPA shifts idiosyncratically from one cohort to the next because of admission-quota discretion, year-to-year program demand and regulated slot supply, so comparing students in the same program and institution across cohorts (net of year effects and cell-specific trends) identifies the effect of peer ability on dropout a
units.source_of_variation: Idiosyncratic cohort-to-cohort variation in the average high school GPA of entering students within education-by-institution cells, 1985-2010, arising from institutions' discretion over quota 1 versus quota 2 admissions, year-to-year variation in demand for specific programs under the deferred-acceptance Coordinated Enrollment System, and regulation of the supply of study slots

units.summary: Peer ability is measured by high school grades fixed before enrollment, so conditioning on individual and peer covariates (and the cell structure) the predetermined peer measure is treated as unrelated to the student's own dropout decision, ruling out reflection and identifying the peer effect on dropout.
units.source_of_variation: Idiosyncratic cohort-to-cohort variation in the average high school GPA of entering students within education-by-institution cells, 1985-2010, arising from institutions' discretion over quota 1 versus quota 2 admissions, year-to-year variation in demand for specific programs under the deferred-acceptance Coordinated Enrollment System, and regulation of the supply of study slots

units.summary: Being a woman-firm-year event in which an employed woman gives birth in the event year (versus an observationally matched event with no birth in that or adjacent years) instruments the number of births actually occurring at the firm, converting the matched birth-timing comparison into a local average effect of an additional birth on the firm's leave days, employment and hiring.
units.instrument: Treatment_e, an indicator for the event being a treatment event
units.source_of_variation: The timing of a female employee's first observed birth: treatment events are woman-firm-baseline-year combinations in which the woman gives birth in the event year (2 years after the baseline year) and not in the adjacent years, matched to observationally equivalent control events in which she does not give birth in the event year, the year before or the year after. Treatment status instruments the number of births at the firm in the event year.

units.summary: Firms where a female employee gives birth in the event year are compared over event time, relative to the baseline year two years before the birth, with observationally equivalent firm-year events in which the same type of employee does not give birth in the event year or the surrounding years, so differences after the event date identify the intent-to-treat effect of a birth on the firm.
units.source_of_variation: The timing of a female employee's birth: treatment events are woman-firm-baseline-year combinations in which the woman gives birth in the event year, matched to observationally equivalent control events in which she does not give birth in the event year or the adjacent years; outcomes are compared over event time with the baseline year t = -2 as the omitted period.

units.summary: Growth in four other high-income countries' imports of each Chinese product, weighted by the firm's lagged product (and destination) sale shares, isolates China's export-supply push and instruments the firm's own exposure to Chinese import competition when estimating its effect on the firm's R&D worker share.
units.instrument: Imp^IV_{it−1} = log( sum_p (sale_{ipt−2}/sale_{it−2}) Imp^{CH-HI}_{pt−1} + 1 ) (Eq. 3): total purchases of product p from China by four high-income countries (Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand), w
units.source_of_variation: Chinese export supply growth, proxied by the imports of Chinese products by four high-income countries (Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand) over 1995-2012, interacted with firm-specific lagged product (and destination) sale shares

units.summary: With firm, sector, municipality and year fixed effects plus lagged firm controls, the estimate comes from year-to-year changes within the same firm in its lagged Chinese import exposure, which firms cannot respond to contemporaneously.
units.source_of_variation: within-firm variation over 1995-2012 in the firm's lagged exposure to Chinese imports in the markets it sells to

units.summary: Employees in an inception cohort are compared by the job-exposure-matrix probability of work-related violence attached to their occupation, with the one-year-lagged exposure assumed independent of depression risk once pre-entry and time-varying covariates are adjusted for.
units.source_of_variation: Between-occupation differences in the job-exposure-matrix probability of work-related violence, as employees move through jobs after entering the workforce. There is no reform, lottery or discontinuity: the design is an observational inception-cohort comparison adjusted for pre-workforce-entry risk factors.

units.summary: The 2010 bracket reform is used to build a simulated instrument — the net-of-tax rate change implied by applying post-reform rules to inflation-adjusted base-year income — which, conditional on pre-reform income controls, isolates variation in high-income workers' net-of-tax rate independent of their own behaviour and identifies the hours elasticity.
units.instrument: Mechanical change in the marginal net-of-tax rate on labor income of high-income workers, log(1 - tau^H_{Mit+3}) - log(1 - tau^H_{it}), where post-reform rates are simulated from base-year income adju
units.source_of_variation: The 2010 Danish personal income tax reform, which abolished the middle bracket of the three-bracket progressive schedule, lowered bottom and top marginal tax rates by 2 and 7 percentage points respectively between 2008 and 2011, and raised the top-bracket threshold by about 9% in real terms; workers' 2008 position in the tax schedule determines exposure. Identification of the spillover uses the firm-level average mechanical change in the net-of-tax rate of high-income coworkers.

units.summary: Changes in the firm-level average regular hours of high-income workers (and their net-of-tax rates) are related to co-workers' hours changes within a sample of workers staying at the same firm, with identification resting on conditioning on observed worker and firm characteristics rather than on a separate source of variation.
units.source_of_variation: The 2010 Danish personal income tax reform, which abolished the middle bracket of the three-bracket progressive schedule, lowered bottom and top marginal tax rates by 2 and 7 percentage points respectively between 2008 and 2011, and raised the top-bracket threshold by about 9% in real terms; workers' 2008 position in the tax schedule determines exposure. Identification of the spillover uses the firm-level average mechanical change in the net-of-tax rate of high-income coworkers.

units.summary: Survey-measured mental well-being in 2016 is linked to register-measured healthcare and sickness benefit costs the following year, with identification resting on regression adjustment for observed covariates including prior-year costs rather than on any exogenous shock.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used: this is a prospective observational cohort in which variation in the 2016 WEMWBS score across survey respondents is related to register-measured costs in 2017, adjusting for observed covariates including costs in the previous year.

units.summary: A 2011 reform raised early, incentivized and full retirement ages by six months only for people born on or after January 1, 1954, so comparing earnings and pension contributions of cohorts born just either side of that birth date isolates the effect of later statutory eligibility.
units.source_of_variation: The May 2011 Danish reform on later retirement, which raised the early retirement age, the incentivized retirement age and the full retirement age by six months - from 60, 62 and 65 to 60.5, 62.5 and 65.5 - for everyone born on or after January 1, 1954, and left them unchanged for those born one day earlier. The first of the reform's stepwise birth-date discontinuities, which the authors call the cleanest quasi-experiment it creates.

units.summary: The same January 1, 1954 birth-date discontinuity in eligibility ages is used within subsamples defined by pre-announcement use of personal plans, so the jump at the cutoff identifies how later eligibility changes personal pension saving for each group.
units.source_of_variation: The May 2011 Danish reform's six-month increase in pension eligibility ages for those born on or after January 1, 1954, estimated separately within subsamples defined by preannouncement use of personal retirement plans.

units.summary: The discontinuity at the January 1, 1954 birth date is estimated both for actual employer-plan contributions and for contributions predicted by pre-reform firm default rates, so the comparison of the two jumps at the cutoff attributes the response to default rules rather than active choice.
units.source_of_variation: The May 2011 reform's six-month increase in pension eligibility ages for those born on or after January 1, 1954; the mechanism exercise compares the RD discontinuity in actual employer-plan contributions with the discontinuity in contributions predicted by 2010 firm default contribution rates.

units.summary: Distributions of individual deviations from the inferred firm default contribution rate are overlaid for cohorts born just before and just after the January 1, 1954 eligibility cutoff in successive years, so any divergence across the cutoff after the reform (and none before it) reveals the reform's effect on active departures from defaults.
units.source_of_variation: The January 1, 1954, birth date cutoff, used descriptively: the distributions of deviations from inferred firm default contribution rates are overlaid for cohorts born before and on or after the cutoff, in each of four years. No regression is estimated; Figure 9 panel A (age 56, preannouncement) serves as the placebo.

units.summary: Monthly densities of benefit claiming and retirement ages are plotted separately for cohorts born just before and just after the January 1, 1954 cutoff, so the six-month shift of the spikes across otherwise identical neighbouring cohorts shows that behaviour tracks the statutory eligibility ages.
units.source_of_variation: The same January 1, 1954, birth date discontinuity created by the May 2011 reform, used here descriptively: the empirical monthly claiming- and retirement-age densities are plotted separately for cohorts born just before the cutoff (unaffected) and just after it (eligibility ages six months higher). No regression is estimated.

units.summary: Mobility statistics are computed from matched parent-child income ranks measured at fixed ages, and an estimated life-cycle income process is simulated to show what those statistics would be if unobserved lifetime income were used instead of the short-run proxy.
units.source_of_variation: Simulation of an estimated income process; the counterfactual is the unobserved lifetime income of the same pairs

units.summary: Siblings sharing the same parental record are compared at the same child age, so differences in median income rank are attributed to birth order with all shared family background held fixed.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in birth order within families identified as sharing an identical parental record, with child age held fixed at 36 or 37

units.summary: Father's income is imputed from his age, province of birth and self-employment income share in a first sample and the prediction is used as regressor in the child's sample, mimicking two-sample two-stage least squares as if parents and children were not directly linked.
units.instrument: father's age, his province of birth, and his share of self-employment income out of total income (education, the usual instrument in this literature, is not observed)
units.source_of_variation: Two-sample two-stage least squares: father's income is imputed from instruments observed in both samples, replicating the procedure used by previous survey-based Italian studies, run 'as if' fathers were not matched to children.

units.summary: The covariance structure of residual log earnings over the short panel dimension of the administrative data identifies the persistence of the permanent component and the variance of transitory shocks in an error-component model.
units.source_of_variation: Estimation of an error-component model on the short panel dimension of the administrative data

units.summary: A thirty-year social-security panel observes lifetime earnings directly, so regressing the three-year average at ages 35-37 on lifetime average earnings in that panel quantifies how well the short-window proxy stands in for permanent income.
units.source_of_variation: A long longitudinal sample (INPS, 1985-2016) that observes individual work histories for over 30 years

units.summary: GPs observed a given number of years before their eventual retirement are compared with GPs who have not retired, conditioning on GP age, patient composition, geography, list size, calendar year and Mundlak GP-level covariate means, so the remaining contrast is interpreted as an association between proximity to retirement and practice style.
units.source_of_variation: Observational contrast between single-handed GPs who retire within 2015-2017, indexed by dummies for the number of years before retirement, and GPs who have not retired by the end of 2017, conditional on GP age (cohort), patient population characteristics, geography, calendar year, list size and Mundlak GP-level means. No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used; the authors describe the estimate as an association.

units.summary: The variances of the latent assortative-mating and family-environment factors are identified by matching the model's correlation equations to observed spouse, parent-child and sibling education correlations in two-parent/two-child family quartets, with the gap between same-gender and mixed-gender sibling correlations (gender composition being quasi-random) pinning down the residual sibling compone
units.source_of_variation: the family-quartet structure (two parents and their first two children) combined with variation in the gender composition of the two children: under restriction (6) the gap between same-gender and mixed-gender sibling correlations identifies the residual sibling component and so closes the otherwise under-identified system of correlation equations ; Panel (C) additionally exploits the cohort structure of the empirical moments

units.summary: Child education is regressed on both parents' education (and their interaction) at once, so that conditioning on the co-parent's schooling is meant to net the assortative-mating component out of each parent's coefficient, leaving an association the authors themselves do not treat as causal.
units.source_of_variation: none exogenous: conditioning on the co-parent's years of education is used, following Holmlund, Lindahl and Plug (2011), to net the assortative-mating component out of each parent's coefficient

units.summary: Only households that eventually experience the same severe health event are used, and those whose event falls five years later serve as the control group, so the effect is identified by when within the window the event happened, under parallel trends.
units.source_of_variation: the timing of the health event within a short window: households of the same cohorts that experience the same event five years apart (event in year tau versus year tau + Delta, Delta = 5) are compared, so that only affected households are used and the treatment effect is identified from when the event was realized

units.summary: Vague eligibility rules let regional councils and municipal caseworkers differ in how generously they award Social DI survivors benefits, so the leave-one-out municipality-by-year mean benefit of other nonworking widows instruments a widow's own benefit receipt in her participation equation.
units.instrument: the leave-one-out municipality-by-year average of survivors benefits received through Social DI by nonworking surviving spouses
units.source_of_variation: spatial and over-time variation in the local administration of Social Disability Insurance: regional councils (15 regions) and municipal caseworkers (270 municipalities) decide on applications, and vague eligibility criteria in nonmedical cases generate substantial variation in rejection rates and in mean benefit receipts across municipalities over time

units.summary: Cancer survivors who report being offered a flexible schedule (or psychological help) are compared with those who were not, with identification resting on regression adjustment for a rich set of survey and register covariates assumed to capture all confounders.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation between cancer survivors in whether the workplace offered a flexible work schedule (and psychological help) during and after cancer treatment, as reported in a 2010 survey linked to Danish administrative data. No reform, instrument, discontinuity or before/after comparison is used; identification rests on controlling for a large set of register- and survey-based covariates.

units.summary: Identification comes from comparing out-migration of residents facing different minority shares in their individualized k-nearest-neighbour neighbourhoods, conditioning on neighbourhood socioeconomic controls, individual characteristics and year dummies, with no reform, instrument or discontinuity.
units.source_of_variation: Observed cross-sectional and over-time variation in the ethnic composition of individualized k-nearest-neighbor neighborhoods among residents of the Copenhagen agglomeration in 2007, 2011 and 2014. No reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used; identification rests on conditioning on observed neighborhood and individual characteristics.

atlas.from_label: Local immigrant share of the workforce

units.summary: Employees whose jobs were outsourced in a given year are compared, in stacked event-time panels, with exactly matched public employees who were not outsourced that year, so the staggered timing of the 73 outsourcing contracts identifies the effect on earnings and transfer receipt under conditional parallel trends.
units.source_of_variation: 73 instances of Danish government outsourcing of cleaning, road and park maintenance, retirement home operations, and canteen and catering services over 2005-2013, which transferred 1,478 public employees to the private vendor winning the contract; the outsourcing year varies across individuals and is stacked into treatment-year panels

units.summary: Cross-individual differences in the educational-attainment polygenic score, conditioned on birth-year, gender, birth order and genetic principal components, are used to estimate the return to genetic human capital, assuming no remaining confounding such as genetic nurture.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-individual variation in the educational-attainment polygenic score in the full iPSYCH analytic sample, conditional on year-of-birth fixed effects, gender, birth order and the first ten principal components of the genetic matrix. The paper calls this the between-family model (Equation 1) and stresses that the polygenic score is not guaranteed to be exogenous.

atlas.to_label: Returns to genetic endowments in education

units.summary: Family fixed effects restrict comparisons to siblings, so only genotype differences that are randomly assigned at conception given parental genotype drive variation in the polygenic score, purging shared family environment and genetic nurture.
units.source_of_variation: Genetic variation across siblings within the same family: conditional on parental genotype, child genotype is randomly assigned at conception, so sibling differences in the polygenic score are independent of any environmental effect shared by siblings. Family fixed effects absorb all shared family influences (within-family model, Equation 2).

atlas.to_label: Returns to genetic endowments in education

units.summary: Identification comes entirely from fitting a doubly constrained logit random-utility model, with i.i.d. extreme-value utility shocks and utility linear in alternative characteristics, to the observed cross-section of residence-workplace municipality pairs, so that cross-pair differences in commuting and housing costs pin down the structural coefficients on the choice probabilities.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation across Danish municipality pairs in 1995 in commuting costs and in characteristics of the potential residence municipality. No reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used: identification rests on the random-utility (logit) model imposed on the observed residence-workplace matrix.

units.summary: Patients whose primary care practice closes at a given date are compared, before and after that date, with patients of practices that close three years later (assigned a synthetic closing date from the observed closure-date distribution), so the staggered timing of closures net of individual and period effects identifies the closure's impact on access and utilization.
units.source_of_variation: The timing of closures of Danish primary care practices over 1998‒2015 (770 closing practices), with patients at practices that close three years later as the comparison group and a synthetic closing date drawn from the empirical distribution of observed closing dates

atlas.to_label: distance to the primary care provider

units.summary: Mothers born just before and just after the August 1957 birth-date cut-off of the 1972 compulsory schooling reform are compared, with the discontinuity in outcomes at the cut-off (net of smooth trends in month of birth) giving the intention-to-treat effect of reform exposure.
units.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for cohorts enrolling in 7th grade by August 1972, i.e. persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

units.summary: The discontinuous jump in maternal schooling at the August 1957 birth-cohort cut-off of the compulsory schooling reform is used as an instrument for maternal years of education in a fuzzy design, identifying its effect on children's birth weight and later hospitalizations for compliers.
units.instrument: The school reform dummy T = 1(r >= 0), equal to one for maternal cohorts born from August 1957 who were subject to 9 rather than 7 years of compulsory schooling, used as an instrument for maternal yea
units.source_of_variation: The Danish compulsory schooling reform of 1972 (Consolidated Act No. 106 of February 3rd, 1972), which raised compulsory schooling from 7 to 9 years for persons born from August 1st 1957 onwards, used as an instrument for maternal years of education; the running variable is the mother's month of birth relative to that cut-off.

units.summary: Child outcomes are regressed on observed maternal years of education conditional on calendar month-of-birth fixed effects and the running-variable polynomial, which the authors present as descriptive associations rather than causal effects because education remains selected on unobservables.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in maternal years of education within maternal calendar month-of-birth cells and net of the running-variable polynomial; the authors describe these estimates as statistical associations, not causal effects.

units.summary: Within municipality-of-birth and birth year-month cells, the continuous index of local respiratory disease prevalence among older children is interacted with being a younger (more susceptible) sibling, so identification comes from how irregular seasonal disease waves differentially affect younger versus older siblings exposed to the same local environment at the same time.
units.source_of_variation: Birth-order variation in susceptibility to intrahousehold respiratory disease spread combined with within-municipality, over-time variation in local respiratory disease prevalence among children aged 13-71 months (driven by irregular seasonal waves of RSV and influenza); the differential effect on younger versus older siblings within municipality of birth and birth year-month.

units.summary: Visit weeks are re-drawn at random 200 times and the treatment/control groups rebuilt, so the event study is re-estimated on timing that carries no real nurse-visit information and should produce no effect on weekly vaccination uptake.
units.source_of_variation: Randomly assigned (placebo) week of the closest nurse visit, drawn 200 times for all families in the sample; treatment and control groups are then rebuilt and the main event study re-estimated.

units.summary: Within a four-week window around week 13, families whose closest universal nurse home visit falls in the two weeks before the recommended vaccination age are compared over event time with those visited in the two weeks after, conditioning on covariates, nurse and birth-year fixed effects so that the exact visit week is as good as random.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the exact week of the closest universal nurse home visit within the four weeks around week 13, the nationally recommended age for the first infant vaccination round: families visited in the two weeks before that week are compared with families visited in the two weeks after it. The variation arises from visit-to-visit scheduling by nurses and families, which the paper argues does not depend on the recommended vaccination ages.

units.summary: Individual fixed effects absorb time-constant ability and recruitability, so only within-person changes over time in the number of coworker ties to listed-firm boards are used to predict a first board seat.
Within-person variation over time in ties to executives of listed firms, net of individual fixed effects, identifies the association with getting a first board seat.
Individual fixed effects leave only within-person changes in coworker ties to listed-firm executives to explain first-time board appointment.
Changes within the same person in ties to executives of large firms, with individual fixed effects removing fixed traits, identify the link to a first board seat.
Only within-person variation in coworker ties to large-firm executives is used, since individual fixed effects absorb time-invariant heterogeneity.
Within-person changes in the count of male coworker board ties, net of individual fixed effects, identify the association with a first board appointment.

atlas.from_label: Male share of the professional network

units.summary: Individual fixed effects restrict the comparison to over-time changes in a person's ties to male executives when predicting a first board seat.
Within-person variation in male coworker-executive ties identifies the appointment relation once time-constant individual attributes are differenced out.
The panel regression with individual fixed effects uses only changes in a person's coworker board network over time to explain first-time appointment.
Interacting gender with the within-person change in coworker board ties, under individual fixed effects, identifies whether women's networks pay off differently.
Individual fixed effects leave within-person growth in executive ties as the variation explaining a first board seat.
The gender interaction with within-person changes in executive ties, net of individual fixed effects, identifies a differential return for women.
Within-person changes in coworker ties to executives identify the appointment relation after individual fixed effects remove fixed recruitability.
Gender interacted with within-person variation in coworker executive ties, under individual fixed effects, identifies the gendered network return.
Within-person transitions into the CEO position, net of individual fixed effects, identify how holding that post relates to a first board seat.
Changes within the same person into other top-executive posts explain first board appointment once individual fixed effects are included.
Accumulation of prior CEO experience within a person's own career history, net of individual fixed effects, identifies its link to first board appointment.
Firm fixed effects compare men and women employed at the same firm, so the estimated gender gap in first board appointment is net of time-constant firm characteristics.
With firm fixed effects, individuals in the same firm who differ in coworker board ties are compared on first board appointment.
Within the same firm, the gender interaction with coworker board ties identifies whether women convert such ties into first appointments less often.
Firm fixed effects hold the employer fixed while individuals differing in executive ties are compared on first board appointment.
The gender interaction with executive ties is estimated among employees of the same firm, netting out time-constant firm factors.
Firm fixed effects restrict comparisons to colleagues at the same firm who differ in coworker ties to executives.
Within firms, gender interacted with coworker executive ties identifies a differential appointment return for women.
Firm fixed effects compare CEOs with other employees of the same firm on the probability of a first board appointment.
Holding other top-executive posts is compared with other positions inside the same firm, with firm fixed effects absorbing employer traits.
Within the same firm, employees differing in prior CEO experience are compared on first board appointment.
Within-person changes in the total board network, net of individual fixed effects, identify the relation to holding any board appointment.
Gender interacted with within-person growth in board ties, under individual fixed effects, identifies whether women's board networks are less valuable for any appointment.
Individual fixed effects leave only over-time changes in coworker board ties to explain appointment to any board seat.

Children whose parent receives a first cancer diagnosis are coarsened-exact-matched one year before onset to otherwise similar children without a parental health shock, so that the unanticipated timing of diagnosis makes exposure as good as random conditional on the matching and baseline control variables.
units.source_of_variation: Onset (first diagnosis) of a cancer in one parent, argued to be unanticipated because the precise timing of the shock is random. Children exposed to parental cancer are coarsened-exact-matched, one year before the diagnosis, to children with no parental health shock on age, gender, area of residence and parental characteristics; severity is measured by cancer-specific 5-year statistical survival rates rather than by individual disease outcomes.

units.summary: Road-network distances from the pupil's age-15 residence to the nearest general and vocational institutions (and their interactions with the 9th grade math score), conditional on cohort, municipality, test scores and family background, shift the probability of choosing vocational schooling and are used as instruments to trace marginal treatment effects of vocational versus general education on lat
units.instrument: Distance to vocational education (km), distance to general education (km), and their cross terms with the 9th grade math test score and an indicator for missing math test score
units.source_of_variation: Geographic variation in the weighted average road-network distances from the student's residence at about age 15 to general and to vocational upper secondary institutions (and, in the main specification, their interactions with the 9th grade math test score), conditional on cohort and 92 municipality of residence dummies, 9th grade test scores and family background. Marginal treatment effects are estimated by a local-IV / control-function approach.

units.summary: Within cohort and municipality cells, and conditional on test scores and family background, pupils living at different road distances from general and vocational institutions are compared in a latent-index choice model to estimate how distance shifts the probability of completing a vocational rather than a general program.
units.instrument: Distance to vocational education (km) and distance to general education (km); in Columns 1 and 3 also their cross terms with the 9th grade math test score and an indicator for missing math test score
units.source_of_variation: Geographic variation in the weighted average road-network distance from the student's residence at about age 15 to general and to vocational upper secondary institutions, conditional on cohort and 92 municipality of residence dummies, 9th grade test scores and family background.

units.summary: Earnings of pupils who completed vocational versus general upper secondary education are compared by OLS conditional on cohort and municipality dummies plus a rich set of family background and 9th grade test score controls, as a selection-on-observables benchmark for the instrumented estimates.
units.source_of_variation: Observational variation in which type of upper secondary program was completed, conditional on 3 cohort dummies, 92 municipality of residence dummies and 62 family background and 9th grade test score variables. No exogenous variation is used; the paper reports these OLS estimates as a benchmark before the MTE analysis.

units.summary: Because birth order fixes how much of early childhood each older sibling shares with the third-born child, the paper differences the first- versus second-born outcome gap between families whose third child is disabled by age five and otherwise comparable families whose third child is not, attributing the differential gap to sibling spillovers.
units.source_of_variation: Birth order within the family determines how much of early childhood a child spends with the third-born sibling; the first- versus second-born gap is compared across families whose third-born child is observed disabled by age five and families whose third-born child is not.

units.summary: Because a disabled third-born sibling arrives earlier in the lives of second-borns than of first-borns, the first-to-second-born gap in achievement within families with a disabled third child is compared with the same birth-order gap in families whose third child is not disabled, with family fixed effects absorbing shared family traits.
units.source_of_variation: differential exposure of the first- and second-born child to a disabled third-born sibling, arising from birth order (and in columns 4–6 from birth spacing), differenced against the same birth-order gap in families whose third child is not disabled; family fixed effects absorb time-invariant family differences

units.summary: The same birth-order-gap difference-in-differences is applied to the two older siblings' birth weight, determined before the third child was born, so any estimated 'effect' would signal differential family trends rather than sibling spillovers.
units.source_of_variation: the same difference-in-differences design as the main estimates, applied to outcomes established before the third child was born, as a test of unconfoundedness

units.summary: The birth-order-gap difference-in-differences is run within groups defined by the mother's education at first birth, so the spillover is identified from the same within-family exposure contrast separately by maternal schooling.
units.source_of_variation: the main difference-in-differences design estimated separately within maternal education groups (measured at the time of the first birth)

units.summary: The same within-family exposure contrast, differenced against families without a disabled third child, is estimated separately for immigrant and native-born mothers.
units.source_of_variation: the main difference-in-differences design estimated separately for families with immigrant and with native-born mothers

units.summary: The birth-order exposure gap across families with and without a disabled third child is estimated with achievement measured in a single grade rather than pooled across grades.
units.source_of_variation: the main difference-in-differences design, with the outcome measured in a single grade instead of pooled across grades 3–8

units.summary: In families with at least five years between the second and third birth, the same birth-order-gap design is applied to the older siblings' own disability status, which is already determined before the third child is born, as a check on confounding.
units.source_of_variation: the same difference-in-differences design applied to an outcome realised before the third child's birth, in the subsample of families with at least five years between the second and third birth

units.outcome: maternal employment at child age two
units.summary: The birth-order-gap difference-in-differences is applied to maternal employment measured when the older children are aged one or two, almost always before the third child's birth, so a null result supports the parallel-trends assumption.
units.source_of_variation: the same difference-in-differences design applied to maternal employment measured when the first two children are age 1 or 2, almost invariably before the third child's birth

units.summary: Stepwise cross-sectional regressions relate parental background (education field, income, living arrangement, inventorship) to children's educational-track and inventorship outcomes, conditioning on observable family and cohort controls rather than on any exogenous shock, so the estimates are conditional correlations along the educational ladder.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation: stepwise cross-sectional regressions of educational outcomes and inventorship on parental background, conditional on the observable controls

units.summary: The paper splits first-born children by whether their second-born sibling is a brother or a sister — a draw it treats as random and independent of family tastes — and fully interacts the parental-background regression with that split, so the difference in the parental coefficients between subsamples identifies heterogeneity in parental transmission to inventorship.
units.source_of_variation: The random occurrence of the gender of the second-born sibling: first-born children with a second-born brother are compared with first-born children with a second-born sister, in a split-sample (fully interacted) design

atlas.from_label: gendered parental expectations about daughters' and sons' returns from inventorship
atlas.to_label: transmission of inventorship from parents to daughters

units.summary: Among all first-borns with a sibling, children with and without the parental characteristic are compared on inventorship conditional on parental education, income, living arrangement, municipality and birth year, providing the pooled selection-on-observables benchmark against which the sibling-gender split-sample estimates are read.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation for this column: a cross-sectional comparison of children with and without the parental characteristic among all first-borns with a sibling, conditional on the observable controls. The column is the pooled reference for the split-sample sibling comparison

units.summary: Treating the sex of the second-born child as a natural experiment, first-borns who happened to get a brother are compared with those who got a sister, and the gap in the parental-inventorship effect on becoming an inventor is read as the causal effect of sibling gender.
units.source_of_variation: The random occurrence of the gender of the second-born sibling, used as a natural experiment: the difference between the parental-inventorship coefficient of first-borns with a second-born brother and that of first-borns with a second-born sister

units.summary: The four-year change in an individual's log marginal net-of-tax rate is instrumented by the change a tax simulator predicts from the 2009-10 reform rules applied to income and characteristics fixed at initial levels, so only the mechanical, reform-driven part of the rate change—conditional on initial income—identifies the elasticity of taxable income.
units.instrument: Predicted between-income change in the log marginal net-of-tax rate, E(Delta ln tau^p_{it-1} | z_{it-1}), computed from a tax simulator holding income and characteristics fixed at their initial levels
units.source_of_variation: The 2009-10 Danish tax reform: the middle tax threshold was raised to the top threshold in 2009 and the middle tax bracket was abolished entirely in 2010, raising the marginal net-of-tax rate by approximately 17 log points for the highest-income individuals while average changes below DKK 350,000 were less than 5 log points.

atlas.to_label: Taxable income reported to the tax authority

units.summary: Income regions hit hard by the 2009-10 reform are compared with near-unaffected regions in how their income trend differentials shift from the pre-reform to the post-reform window, with an untreated validation region used to check that trend differentials would otherwise have stayed constant.
units.source_of_variation: The 2009-10 Danish tax reform: in 2009 the middle tax threshold was raised to the level of the top threshold and in 2010 the middle tax bracket was abolished entirely, raising the marginal net-of-tax rate by approximately 17 log points for the highest-income individuals while leaving the bottom of the distribution close to unaffected.

units.summary: Simulated reform-induced changes in the log marginal net-of-tax rate instrument the actual rate change separately across segments of the income distribution, yielding income-region-specific elasticities of taxable income under the assumption that trend differentials are stable absent the reform.
units.source_of_variation: The 2009-10 Danish tax reform: in 2009 the middle tax threshold was raised to the level of the top threshold and in 2010 the middle tax bracket was abolished entirely, raising the marginal net-of-tax rate by approximately 17 log points for the highest-income individuals while leaving the bottom of the distribution close to unaffected.

units.summary: The same simulated-instrument strategy is applied to the 2004 reform, where raising the middle-tax threshold mechanically changed marginal net-of-tax rates most for a specific income band, and this predicted change instruments the realised rate change in an income-growth regression.
units.source_of_variation: The 2004 Danish tax reform, whose main element was a significant increase in the middle tax income threshold, producing the largest predicted changes in marginal net-of-tax rates for personal income between DKK 290,000 and DKK 360,000.

units.summary: For the 2004 reform, income groups whose marginal net-of-tax rates were predicted to change most are compared with little-affected groups in the pre- to post-reform shift of their income trend differentials, with an untreated validation region serving as a falsification check.
units.source_of_variation: The 2004 Danish tax reform, whose main element was a significant increase in the middle tax income threshold, producing the largest predicted changes in marginal net-of-tax rates for personal income between DKK 290,000 and DKK 360,000.

units.summary: The 1987 reform changed marginal net-of-tax rates unevenly across the income distribution, and taxable income responses are read off the pre- to post-reform change in trend differentials between more- and less-exposed income regions.
units.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, one of the four major reforms since 1980 highlighted in Fig. 2.

units.summary: Cross-country differences in deep-rooted genetic distance to the frontier population are related to income inequality, with geographic and agroclimatic controls plus world-region dummies assumed to render that distance as good as randomly assigned.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-country (or country-pair) variation in deep-rooted genetic distance, a proxy for the time elapsed since two populations separated from a common ancestor

units.summary: The association between ancestral genetic distance and inequality is split into the portion transmitted by redistribution policy, treating redistribution as conditionally exogenous given geography, region dummies and the proximate determinants.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-country (or country-pair) variation in deep-rooted genetic distance, a proxy for the time elapsed since two populations separated from a common ancestor

units.summary: Genetic distance measured for 1500CE populations, predetermined with respect to modern outcomes, instruments present-day genetic relatedness and is assumed to affect inequality only through it.
units.instrument: Gdist_1500 (log genetic distance to the English population in 1500CE)
units.source_of_variation: Cross-country (or country-pair) variation in deep-rooted genetic distance, a proxy for the time elapsed since two populations separated from a common ancestor

units.summary: Graduates who held different types of student jobs are compared on later earnings and job skill level, conditioning on field and level of study, exit cohort and calendar year, high school track and GPA, and parental background, with identification resting on conditional mean independence rather than any exogenous shock.
units.source_of_variation: Variation across individuals, within level and field of higher education, in the type of student job held while enrolled (high-skill vs low-skill; above vs below median study-relevance). No reform, lottery or discontinuity is used; the authors call the analysis descriptive.

units.summary: Because the collectively negotiated minimum wage jumps discontinuously when a worker turns 18 while everything else evolves smoothly in age, the drop in monthly employment at the 18th birthday identifies the employment effect of the wage floor.

units.summary: Outcomes of boys who entered the summer camp plus one-year mentoring programme are compared between grade 8 (before) and grade 9 (after) against non-participants reweighted by entropy balancing to the participants' covariate means, so the camp's effect is the differential change under conditional parallel trends and no anticipation.
