units.summary: The unforeseeable onset of type 1 diabetes in a sibling is treated as a quasi-random disability shock, and each affected focal child is compared with five untreated focal children matched exactly on birth year, sibling spacing and completed family size, so that differences in graduation and exam performance are attributed to the sibling's disability.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the incidence and timing of type 1 diabetes onset among the siblings of focal children, treated as a quasi-random disability shock; each treated focal child is matched without replacement to five untreated focal children on birth year, sibling spacing and completed family size.

units.summary: Workers at manufacturing plants that shut down entirely are compared with similar non-displaced workers around the closure year, so the timing of an employer-level closure rather than individual choice drives job loss and traces out unemployment and earnings paths.
units.source_of_variation: Full plant closures in Danish manufacturing 1995-2006 (a workplace with at least five workers losing 90% or more of its workers between t-3 and t), a firm-level shock that makes the job loss and its timing plausibly exogenous to the individual

units.summary: The raw male-female difference in post-displacement unemployment and earnings changes is split, by a linear Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition, into the share attributable to differing pre-displacement characteristics and a residual attributed to differing returns, with no exogenous variation involved.
units.source_of_variation: None: a Kitagawa (1955)-Oaxaca (1973)-Blinder (1973) decomposition of the observed male-female difference among displaced workers into a part explained by observable characteristics and a part attributed to different returns to those characteristics

units.summary: Competing-risks hazard models compare union formation across 120 national origin groups differing in dominant religion, value distance and language, with identification resting on conditioning on other cultural traits, local partner-market opportunity structures, generation, education, province and time rather than on any exogenous shock.
units.source_of_variation: Between-country-of-origin variation across 120 national origin groups in dominant religion, Inglehart–Welzel value distance from Denmark and language group, plus year-to-year variation in opportunity structures (relative group size, within-group sex ratio, within-group educational similarity) within the 11 Danish provinces. No reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used; identification rests on conditioning on the observed covariates.

units.summary: Children whose parent's plant closes are matched to otherwise similar untreated children and compared in differences around the closure, with the childhood stage at which the closure hits providing the variation and children already past compulsory schooling (17-22) netting out any remaining selection.
units.source_of_variation: Plant closures and major downsizings at private-sector plants in Denmark, 1986-2017 (51,002 events), identified from matched employer-employee registers; the child's age in the closure year determines the childhood stage of exposure, and children aged 17-22 at closure (for whom the shock cannot affect end-of-school outcomes) serve as the within-design reference group.

units.summary: Workers separating from an establishment that sheds at least 30 percent of its employment are tracked in event time relative to the layoff year and compared with propensity-score-matched non-displaced workers, so the timing of the involuntary separation identifies its effect on earnings, employment and wages.
units.source_of_variation: Job displacement through a mass layoff: separation from the main employer in t* combined with a drop of at least 30 percent in establishment employment in t*; displaced workers are compared with 1:1 propensity-score-matched workers who do not experience such an event. For column 1 the dependent variable is the employer wage premium estimated in a separate AKM first step.

units.summary: The same matched event-study around the mass-layoff separation is used to measure the post-displacement change in the worker's AKM employer wage premium, and that change is expressed as the share of the estimated log wage loss attributable to moving to a lower-paying employer.
units.source_of_variation: Job displacement through a mass layoff, as in equation (1); the quantity reported is a decomposition of the estimated wage loss into the part attributable to the change in the employer's estimated AKM wage premium.

units.summary: Household earnings are tracked in event time around the first child's birth (reference year t-1) and the trajectories of coarsened-exact-matched female same-sex and different-sex couples are contrasted, so the earnings consequences of parenthood are attributed to couple type under the assumption that sexual orientation is unrelated to specialization potential.
units.source_of_variation: The timing of the birth of the couple's first child (event time, reference the year before birth), interacted with couple type, on a Coarsened-Exact-Matched sample of female same-sex and different-sex couples.

units.source_of_variation: The timing of the birth of the couple's first child, with household earnings in the year before birth as the reference and the counterfactual given by predicted earnings at the same age and calendar year in the absence of children.

units.summary: Coarsened Exact Matching on the child's birth year, both partners' ages and both partners' pre-parenthood labor earnings builds a comparable set of different-sex couples for each female same-sex couple, so remaining earnings differences are attributed to couple type conditional on these observables.

units.source_of_variation: Couple type, within strata defined by the couple's eventual number of children.

units.summary: Panel income data are simulated from a calibrated incomplete-markets life-cycle model whose income-process parameters are known by construction, so the quasidifference minimum-distance estimates obtained under alternative weighting schemes can be compared directly with the truth.
units.source_of_variation: data simulated from a calibrated standard incomplete-markets lifecycle model whose true parameters are known by construction

units.source_of_variation: designed Monte Carlo variation: the authors set the true persistence, the variances of fixed effects and of persistent and transitory shocks, the number of individuals, the number of periods, the initial conditions and the weighting scheme, and compare the resulting estimate with the known truth

units.summary: Because the three true variances of the simulated income process are chosen by the authors across simulation cells, the Monte Carlo bias of the estimated persistence can be regressed on those designer-set variances to see which features of the data-generating process drive the bias.
units.source_of_variation: designed Monte Carlo variation: the three true variances are set by the authors across the simulation cells of Tables 1–2, and the bias is observed against the known truth

units.summary: Holding the panel dimensions and all other parameters fixed, the authors raise the variance of the persistent component in the first simulated sample year and inspect how the minimum-distance objective function over the persistence grid changes, which is possible only because the data are simulated from a known process.
units.source_of_variation: designed Monte Carlo variation in the variance of the persistent component in the first sample year, holding N, T and the other parameters fixed

units.summary: Children whose date of birth (and hence the date they reach the relevant vaccination age) falls just after the 2019 reform cut-offs are enrolled in prospective reminders while those just before stay under the old rules, so comparing vaccination uptake across the unmanipulable birth-date threshold identifies the reminder effect.
units.source_of_variation: The 1 August 2019 (date of birth) and 1 November 2019 (turning four and turning 12) cut-offs for enrolment into the new prospective reminder policy; control children remained under the 2017 retrospective digital reminder rules.

units.summary: Children reaching the follow-up ages of 2, 6.5 or 14 just on or after the 15 May 2014 start of the national postal reminder system are reminded while those reaching them just before are not, and the jump in vaccination coverage at that date threshold identifies the letters' effect.
units.source_of_variation: The 15 May 2014 implementation date of the national retrospective postal reminder system: children who turned 2, 6.5 or 14 years on or after that date had their (non-adherent) families reminded; children reaching the same ages before the date did not.

units.summary: Children hitting the follow-up ages on or after the 6 February 2017 switch-over date received the reminder digitally rather than by post, so the discontinuity in coverage at this birth-date-driven cut-off identifies the effect of the delivery channel.
units.source_of_variation: The 6 February 2017 introduction date for digital reminders: children reaching the follow-up ages of 2, 6.5 or 14 years on or after that date had non-adherent families reminded digitally in 'eboks' rather than by post.

units.summary: A temporary cap on total family child benefits cut transfers only for families with particular numbers and ages of children, so labour supply of these mechanically affected families is compared before and after the cap with otherwise similar uncapped families.
units.source_of_variation: The DKK 35,000 cap on total family child benefits, announced in May 2010 and applied to payments from January 2011, repealed from 2012. It cut benefits only for families with more and younger children (three-child families with at least one child under 3 or at least two children under 7, and all families with four or more children), and was based solely on the number and age composition of children, not on family income or labour market status.

units.summary: Children born just before and just after the date-of-birth cutoffs for free HPV vaccination are compared, since birth timing cannot be manipulated around the cutoff, so eligibility (and its spillover to older siblings' take-up) is locally as good as random.
units.source_of_variation: Date-of-birth eligibility cutoffs for the free-of-charge national HPV vaccination programs: girls born on or after January 1, 1993 became eligible when the program was introduced on October 1, 2008, while girls born earlier had to pay about 560 USD; boys born on or after January 1, 2006 became eligible under the 2020 program.

units.summary: The focal younger sibling's own vaccination is instrumented by their date-of-birth eligibility for the free programme, scaling the discontinuity in the older sibling's take-up into a local spillover effect of one sibling's vaccination on the other's.
units.instrument: Eligibility of the focal girl for the 2008 HPV vaccination program, 1[date of birth >= January 1, 1993]
units.source_of_variation: Date-of-birth eligibility cutoffs for the free-of-charge national HPV vaccination programs: girls born on or after January 1, 1993 became eligible when the program was introduced on October 1, 2008, while girls born earlier had to pay about 560 USD; boys born on or after January 1, 2006 became eligible under the 2020 program.

units.summary: Weekly first-dose initiation of eligible versus just-ineligible children (and of their older siblings) is traced in the weeks around the programme's start date, so the dynamics of take-up and of the sibling spillover are read off the eligibility-by-week interaction.
units.source_of_variation: Date-of-birth eligibility cutoffs for the free-of-charge national HPV vaccination programs: girls born on or after January 1, 1993 became eligible when the program was introduced on October 1, 2008, while girls born earlier had to pay about 560 USD; boys born on or after January 1, 2006 became eligible under the 2020 program.

units.summary: In an observational register cohort, the effect of depression on family dissolution is identified by sequentially adjusting at each of five annual time-points for all measured common causes (plus positivity), with LTMLE estimating counterfactual dissolution risks under dynamic antidepressant-treatment regimes.
units.source_of_variation: None designed: an observational register cohort. Identification rests on sequential randomization (all common causes of the depression-dissolution association measured and adjusted for at each of the five annual time-points) together with positivity, with LTMLE used to estimate counterfactual risks under dynamic antidepressant-treatment regimes.

units.summary: The employment–health gradient fitted on 50–54-year-olds, who cannot yet take early retirement, is applied to the observed health and characteristics of each older age group, and the gap between the predicted and the actual employment rate is reported as untapped work capacity.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation. The two-stage Cutler, Meara and Richards-Shubik (2013) health-capacity-to-work method: a covariate-adjusted employment–health gradient estimated on 50–54-year-olds (an age window not yet eligible for early retirement) is applied out of sample to the observed health and characteristics of the older age group, and the gap between that counterfactual employment rate and the actual one is reported as additional work capacity.

units.summary: The same out-of-sample prediction exercise is run separately by education quartile, with the stage-one employment–health regression re-estimated within each socio-economic group, so the predicted-minus-actual employment gap can differ across education levels.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation. The two-stage Cutler, Meara and Richards-Shubik (2013) health-capacity-to-work method, with the stage-one employment regression re-estimated within the subgroup so that the health–employment relationship may vary across socio-economic status.

units.summary: Among 50–54-year-olds, whose employment is not yet shaped by early-retirement availability, the effect of health on employment is read off cross-sectional differences in the health index conditional on education, marital status, country of birth, area of residence and survey wave.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the health index among 50–54-year-olds, an age window chosen because their employment decision is not influenced by the availability of early retirement. There is no reform, instrument or discontinuity: identification rests on the covariate set.

units.summary: The same covariate-adjusted cross-sectional comparison of health and employment among 50–54-year-olds is estimated within the highest education quartile, allowing the health–employment relationship to vary with socio-economic status.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in the health index among 50–54-year-olds within the 4th education quartile; the employment regression is re-estimated by educational attainment so that the health–employment relationship may vary with socio-economic status.

units.summary: The between-wave change in the health index is added as a covariate to the stage-one employment regression before the out-of-sample prediction, so that the predicted-minus-actual employment gap reflects health deterioration as well as the level of health.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation. The same two-stage health-capacity method with the between-wave change in the health index added as a covariate to the stage-one employment regression, to see whether changes in health and not just the level of health shape work capacity.

units.summary: Identification rests on ignorability: women are reweighted by a propensity score over LASSO-selected labor market observables to have men's application behavior, and the resulting change in the segregation index of hiring outcomes is attributed to application behavior rather than to unobserved differences.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional variation in application behavior among men and women with the same LASSO-selected labor market observables; no experimental or quasi-experimental variation is claimed

units.summary: Within the propensity-score reweighted and trimmed sample, men and women with the same observables and the same counterfactual application behavior are compared, so the remaining gender gap in occupation-specific hiring shares is read as the part not explained by where people apply.
units.source_of_variation: none: a gender comparison (or a cross-job-type comparison) within a propensity-score reweighted sample; no experimental or quasi-experimental variation is claimed

units.summary: An overlapping-generations life-cycle model calibrated to the pre-reform year is simulated along its transition path with and without individual elements of the mandated pension contribution reform, so the difference between the full model and each muted counterfactual gives that element's effect on simulated wealth inequality.
units.source_of_variation: Simulated policy variation inside a calibrated overlapping-generations life-cycle model of the Danish economy: the trend increase in mandated fully-funded (occupational) pension contribution rates along the annual transition path between the 1970 and 2100 steady states. Counterfactual worlds mute single reform elements from 1992 onward: (b) no trend in pi_bar, (c) no income-dependent contributions, (d) no change in the PAYG rate.

units.summary: Cross-sectional survey respondents who differ in self-reported well-being and health-related quality of life are compared on their registered GP utilisation, with identification resting entirely on regression adjustment for observed sociodemographics (and prior GP use) rather than any exogenous variation.
units.source_of_variation: No design-based variation: cross-sectional between-person variation in self-reported SWB and HRQoL among 2019 survey respondents, adjusted by regression for observed sociodemographics and (columns 5-6) for GP utilisation predating the survey. The authors call the study exploratory.

units.summary: Identification rests on cross-firm and cross-individual differences in within-level wage dispersion (and firm size and decentralization) among 2002 new hires, assuming that conditional on firm and worker controls, industry and year dummies these differences are unrelated to unobserved determinants of separation.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-firm and cross-individual variation in horizontal wage dispersion (Gini of Mincer-residual and of predicted wages within hierarchical levels), firm size and decentralization among Danish private-sector employees newly hired in 2002. units.summary: The 2006/2007 Danish law mandating gender-segregated wage statistics in larger firms provides a dated, exogenous increase in pay transparency, and separations before versus after the reform are compared across firms with differently sized wage dispersion and size exposure.

units.summary: A coherent Li-Lee mortality model estimated on register death rates by sex and income quartile is used to forecast mortality to 2040, and the same forecast is evaluated under a fixed retirement age of 65 versus the indexed statutory schedule, so the contrast comes entirely from the model-implied policy scenario rather than from data variation.

units.summary: The paper contrasts the historically observed path of survival to age 65 with the paths of survival to the indexed statutory retirement age implied by two coherent mortality forecasting models, so identification of the policy's distributional consequences rests on the fitted forecast models rather than on observed variation.
units.source_of_variation: No variation in the data: the historical observed trajectory of survival to age 65 is compared with the forecast trajectory of survival to the indexed statutory retirement age under two coherent mortality forecasting models.

units.summary: Identification rests on comparing head-and-neck cancer patients who differ in age and tumour stage within a logistic model that adjusts for topography, stage, performance status and comorbidity, assuming no remaining confounding of vaccination uptake.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation between patients in the cohort, adjusted for age at cancer diagnosis, topography, cancer stage, performance status and the Charlson Comorbidity Index.

units.summary: Identification compares patients of different ages within the same Charlson Comorbidity Index stratum via an age-by-comorbidity interaction in the covariate-adjusted logistic model, assuming the conditional age association is unconfounded.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in age between patients within a Charlson Comorbidity Index stratum, in a logistic regression containing an age-by-CCI interaction.

units.summary: Comparing siblings who share family background, the within-family education gradient in health is estimated with and without measured personality traits, and an order-invariant decomposition attributes the change in the gradient to each skill block.

units.summary: Worker and firm fixed effects in a panel of repeated observations let the paper track how an immigrant's wage and the wage premium of the firm employing him change as he passes five years of residence, including for workers who cross the threshold without changing firm, with natives providing the age and year profile.

units.outcome: Firm sorting share of wage gap
units.summary: Workers moving between firms identify group-specific firm wage premiums in an AKM model, so the immigrant-native wage gap at each year since arrival can be decomposed into a firm-sorting component and a worker-fixed-effect component.
units.source_of_variation: Within-worker variation in years since arrival combined with worker mobility between firms, which is what identifies the group-specific firm wage premiums psi_j^S of the AKM model in Eq. (5)

units.summary: Immigrants observed repeatedly in the registers are followed as years since arrival accumulate, with age and calendar-year effects estimated on natives netted out, so the remaining within-immigrant profile traces the assimilation path of the earnings, wage and employment gaps.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in years since arrival within immigrant workers observed repeatedly in the Danish registers 1985-2017, after removing the age and calendar-year effects estimated on the native sample

units.summary: Within the survey, the affective valence of each recall cue and the valence of the experience respondents were asked to recall were independently randomised, so the difference in how often a congruent financial cue is reported as influencing recall is causal.
units.source_of_variation: Within-survey randomisation of the affective valence of each cue and of whether the respondent was asked about recalling positive or negative experiences (and high or low inflation)

units.treatment: family ER visit in survey month
units.summary: Because respondents are freshly sampled at random each month, whether a family emergency-room visit happens to fall in the interview month is random once the household's overall propensity to visit the ER is controlled for, identifying the effect of a salient household shock on inflation beliefs.
units.source_of_variation: Random monthly sampling of survey respondents by Statistics Denmark, which makes the proximity between the interview month and a family emergency-room visit random, holding the household's total number of ER visits fixed

units.summary: Respondent fixed effects across the two Michigan Survey interviews about six months apart absorb persistent optimism, so only within-person changes in expected personal finances are related to changes in the inflation forecast.
units.source_of_variation: Within-respondent variation across the two Michigan Survey interviews, roughly six months apart

units.summary: Preference parameters estimated from the household budget set are used to re-solve the leave-choice model under a hypothetical earmarked-leave reform and read off fathers' predicted take-up.
units.source_of_variation: Counterfactual variation in the parental leave benefit function B(.) imposed on the estimated household model, whose preference parameters are identified from sharp kinks in the Danish household budget set

units.summary: The estimated household model is simulated over a grid of replacement rates, earmarked weeks and total benefit weeks to trace how fathers' leave responds to each policy dimension.
units.source_of_variation: Counterfactual variation in the replacement rate, the number of earmarked weeks and the total number of benefit weeks imposed on the estimated household model

units.outcome: marginal willingness to pay for leave
units.summary: Parents' marginal willingness to pay for leave is backed out of their responses to the sharp kinks the two-tier Danish leave system puts in the household budget set.
units.source_of_variation: Sharp kinks in the household budget set created by the Danish two-tier parental leave system: the exhaustion of each parent's individual, firm-provided wage compensation and the joint exhaustion of the 32 weeks of shared public parental leave benefits

atlas.from_label: Marginal cost of a day of parental leave

units.treatment: kink in marginal cost of leave
units.outcome: excess mass of leave at kink
units.summary: Excess mass in leave lengths at the points where firm wage compensation or shared public benefits run out identifies parents' responsiveness to the price of leave.
units.source_of_variation: Sharp kinks in the household budget set: the exhaustion of a parent's individual, firm-provided wage compensation (fathers) and the joint exhaustion of the 32 weeks of shared public parental leave benefits (mothers)

units.summary: Conditional on a father's own entitlement and sector, the share of his co-workers holding the same entitlement is related to his bunching, so any correlation would indicate peer rather than budget-set responses.
units.source_of_variation: Heterogeneity in fathers' right to wage compensation among co-workers in the same public-sector firm, created by the 6-6-6(7) model: a father whose partner does not work in the same public sub-sector can use the 6 shared weeks uncontested and so has an individual right to 12 weeks

units.summary: National inflows by origin country, interacted with each municipality's 1993 origin-specific settlement pattern (shaped by the refugee dispersal policy that ignored local conditions), predict the local non-Western worker share and instrument its effect on firms' robot adoption.
units.instrument: Shift-share predicted non-Western immigrant share, Img IV^{non-west}_{mt} = sum_d (F_dt / F_d93) * (F_md93 / P_m93)
units.source_of_variation: time and geographic variation in the share of non-Western migrant workers across 94 Danish municipalities 1995-2019, driven by political turmoil and wars abroad and by the Danish Refugee Spatial Dispersal Policy, which until the mid-1990s allocated refugees to municipalities without regard to their characteristics or local economic conditions

atlas.from_label: Local immigrant share of the workforce

units.summary: Within-firm changes over time in the local immigrant share, net of firm, industry and year fixed effects and controls, are related to robot adoption under conditional ignorability, with the Western immigrant share as a comparison treatment.
units.source_of_variation: time and geographic variation in the share of non-Western migrant workers across 94 Danish municipalities 1995-2019, driven by political turmoil and wars abroad and by the Danish Refugee Spatial Dispersal Policy, which until the mid-1990s allocated refugees to municipalities without regard to their characteristics or local economic conditions

atlas.from_label: Local immigrant share of the workforce

units.summary: Cross-municipality and cross-wave differences in the local non-Western immigrant share among surveyed firms are related to reported robot usage conditional on observables, an association the paper does not read causally.
units.source_of_variation: cross-municipality and cross-wave variation in the non-Western immigrant share among VITA respondents

atlas.from_label: Local immigrant share of the workforce

units.summary: Immigrant and native workers are compared within the same firm, industry, occupation, gender and year cells, conditioning on age and education, to measure the immigrant wage gap.
units.source_of_variation: cross-worker comparison within firm, industry, occupation and gender cells

units.summary: Within-municipality variation over time in average non-Western immigrant wages, net of municipality and year fixed effects, is correlated with the local value of robots, without a causal claim.
units.source_of_variation: within-municipality variation over time in average immigrant wages

units.summary: The same shift-share predicted immigrant share instruments the realized local non-Western worker share in the survey sample, identifying its effect on firms' self-reported robot usage.
units.instrument: Shift-share predicted non-Western immigrant share, Img IV^{non-west}_{mt} = sum_d (F_dt / F_d93) * (F_md93 / P_m93)
units.source_of_variation: cross-municipality and cross-wave variation in the non-Western immigrant share among VITA respondents

units.summary: Identification rests on comparing adolescents whose December 2009 address fell in a listed vulnerable housing area with those elsewhere, assuming that conditioning on observed individual and family covariates makes this exposure independent of later NEET status, with the decade-long lag ruling out reverse causation.
units.source_of_variation: Observed cross-sectional variation in December 2009 addresses across the 29 areas on the 2010 Danish governmental list of particularly vulnerable housing areas versus all other micro-areas; no reform, lottery or discontinuity is exploited.

atlas.from_label: living in a vulnerable neighbourhood in adolescence
atlas.to_label: risk of not being in education or employment in emerging adulthood

units.summary: The wage penalty is read off a cross-sectional comparison of workers with and without an imprisonment record, conditioning on education, age, full-time status and year, with no exogenous variation in record status.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used: a cross-sectional comparison of individuals with and without an incarceration record during 1986-2003, conditional on education, a quadratic in age, full-time status and year fixed effects.

units.summary: Poisson search-model transition rates are identified by maximum likelihood from the observed durations of employment and unemployment spells and their realised exit destinations, separately for workers with and without records.
units.source_of_variation: Observed employment spell durations and realised transition destinations (job-to-job, to unemployment, to jail) of the two record groups, fitted by maximum likelihood to the model's Poisson structure.

units.summary: The ex-offender wage gap is generated inside the calibrated search model, where prejudiced firms screen out ex-offenders so that offers come only from the higher-wage-posting unprejudiced majority of firms.
units.source_of_variation: Equilibrium of the calibrated search-and-matching model: ex-offenders receive offers only from unprejudiced firms, which post higher wages when they are a majority (φ = .69).

units.summary: Two calibrated versions of the same search model, differing only in whether firm productivity is heterogeneous, are each simulated and their implied wage distributions compared visually against the same empirical residual CDF.
units.source_of_variation: Comparison of two calibrated versions of the same model (homogeneous versus heterogeneous firm productivity) against the same empirical residual distribution.

units.summary: The calibrated model's equilibrium wage distributions are held up against the observed CDFs of Mincerian wage residuals for each record group, so identification rests on the estimated transition rates and calibrated parameters being correct.
units.source_of_variation: Comparison of the calibrated model's equilibrium wage distributions with the empirical wage residual distributions, separately by record group (Fig. 2).

units.summary: With free universal vaccination for all Danes aged 65+ and thus no reform, lottery or cutoff, identification comes from comparing dementia incidence rates of vaccinated versus unvaccinated person-time in a log-linear Poisson model adjusted for age, sex, calendar year, marital status, education and nine comorbidities, assuming no remaining confounding.
units.source_of_variation: Observed differences in influenza vaccination uptake between older Danes in a nationwide cohort; vaccination has been offered free of charge to all Danish citizens aged >=65 since 2002, so there is no reform, lottery or discontinuity - identification rests entirely on adjustment for measured confounders

units.summary: Because the Danish school-entry rule ties school start to birth year, children born just after January 1 are the oldest rather than the youngest in their cohort, so comparing ADHD prescription rates for births immediately on either side of the cutoff identifies the effect of relative age in class.
units.source_of_variation: The Danish school-entry rule: children should start school in the calendar year they turn six, so children born December 31 should enter school a full year earlier than children born one day later on January 1, making the former the youngest and the latter the oldest in their class. The paper estimates the reduced form of a fuzzy RD design at this January 1 birth-date cutoff.

atlas.from_label: Relative age within the school cohort

units.summary: Managers' self-reported pre-appointment working hours are related to the probability of a subsequent top-management appointment among managers made observationally comparable on a rich set of individual and firm covariates, with identification resting on the absence of remaining confounders rather than on any reform or instrument.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional and over-time variation in self-reported weekly working hours among managers who are observationally comparable on a comprehensive set of individual and firm covariates; there is no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument

units.summary: The raw male-female difference in annual appointment odds is estimated and then re-estimated with successive blocks of individual and firm covariates, so the decline in the female coefficient across steps shows how much of the gender gap each observed block accounts for.
units.source_of_variation: cross-sectional differences between male and female managers in the merged DLFS-IDA sample; covariate blocks are added sequentially to see how much of the raw gender gap each accounts for

units.summary: Appointment probability is purged of all covariates except hours and the resulting residual profile against hours is plotted separately for men and women, so any gender difference in the covariate-adjusted hours-career gradient is read off the two profiles and their confidence bands.
units.source_of_variation: difference between men and women in the covariate-adjusted relationship between hours and appointment odds; no exogenous variation in hours is used

units.summary: Female-by-hours interaction terms are added to the covariate-adjusted appointment regression, so a gender difference in the return to working hours would appear as significant interactions conditional on the same observables.
units.source_of_variation: differences between men and women in the covariate-adjusted hours gradient

units.summary: The estimated dynamic model of couples' labour supply, home production, savings and divorce is re-simulated for 20,000 synthetic couples with the maintenance-policy parameters changed and all other structural parameters held fixed, so the simulated difference is the policy's causal effect within the model.
units.source_of_variation: Counterfactual re-simulation of the estimated dynamic structural model under alternative maintenance-policy parameters, holding the estimated structural parameters fixed; N = 20,000 simulated couples.

units.summary: Because couples divorce in different calendar years and at different ages, event-time coefficients around the divorce year — net of age and year fixed effects in a balanced register panel — trace out the changes in hours, wages and wealth attributable to divorce rather than to ageing or common time trends.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in the timing of divorce across Danish couples observed in administrative registers 1980-2013, with age and calendar-year fixed effects absorbing age and time trends (specification (1), following Kleven et al. 2019).

units.summary: The CES home-production and utility parameters are identified by choosing them so that the simulated model reproduces 89 empirical moments on hours, home production, wages and divorce from Danish registers and the time-use survey, with the functional-form and moment-matching restrictions doing the identifying work.
units.source_of_variation: Method-of-simulated-moments fit of the dynamic structural model to 89 empirical moments computed from Danish register data 1980-2013 and the 2001 Danish Time Use Survey.

units.summary: Because a municipal allocation program matches urgent-need applicants to vacant social housing by referral date and unit characteristics rather than by applicant preferences, the neighborhood quality of the first offered unit is quasi-random conditional on application characteristics and is used to instrument the quality of the neighborhood actually moved into.
units.instrument: Index of neighborhood quality of the FIRST assigned housing unit (wi), instrumenting the neighborhood quality of the accepted housing unit (zi)
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of 'urgent needs' households to municipal social housing units by the Municipality of Copenhagen, 2009-2014: every third vacant unit is reserved for urgent-need households and the allocation program picks the waiting applicant with the oldest referral date among those matching the unit's characteristics

units.summary: Conditioning on the exact household application characteristics the allocation program uses to match applicants to vacant units, the remaining differences in assigned neighborhood quality across similar urgent-need households are treated as unrelated to potential outcomes, identifying neighborhood effects by regression adjustment.
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random assignment of 'urgent needs' households to municipal social housing units by the Municipality of Copenhagen, 2009-2014: every third vacant unit is reserved for urgent-need households and the allocation program picks the waiting applicant with the oldest referral date among those matching the unit's characteristics

units.summary: Because the asset test only looks at end-of-December liquid wealth, cash withdrawals of those just below the threshold are compared across months and against age-ineligible 60-64 singles, whose monthly pattern is flat.
units.source_of_variation: the interaction of the end-of-year timing of the asset test with the position of end-of-year liquid wealth relative to the threshold, compared across months and against the age-ineligible 60-64 control group

units.summary: The 1941-1945 cohorts are followed as they cross the statutory retirement age, and their indexed liquid wealth distribution at ages 70-74 is compared with their own distribution at ages 60-64 before the asset test applied.
units.source_of_variation: the panel dimension of the registers: the same cohorts born 1941-1945 are followed as they age into eligibility at the statutory retirement age of 65, and their liquid wealth distribution at ages 70-74 is compared with their own distribution at ages 60-64 (a cohort approach, described by the authors as a simple difference rather than a difference-in-differences)

units.summary: Excess mass just below the DKK 90,000 notch is compared across eligible age groups that differ in time since crossing age 65, using the age-ineligible 60-64 group as the counterfactual density.
units.source_of_variation: variation in time since crossing the statutory age threshold of 65, in a pooled 2014-2018 cross-section of low-income singles, against the DKK 90,000 asset test notch

units.summary: The asset test creates a notch in the budget set at DKK 90,000, and excess mass in the liquid wealth density just below it for age- and income-eligible singles, relative to smooth ineligible densities, identifies the behavioural response.
units.source_of_variation: variation in eligibility for the old-age check coming from the statutory age threshold (65) and the income phaseout, combined with the notch in the budget set created by the DKK 90,000 asset test

units.summary: The 2003 introduction of the asset-tested old-age check dates the appearance of excess mass below the threshold, comparing the eligible group's wealth density in 2001-2002 with 2003-2007.
units.source_of_variation: the introduction of the old-age check and its asset test in 2003

units.summary: High-frequency bank data for treated individuals below the threshold show December spikes in spending and debt repayment relative to their other months, the mechanism by which end-of-year wealth is pushed below the test.
units.source_of_variation: the end-of-year timing of the asset test, applied to high-frequency bank measures of spending and debt repayment for the treated group below the threshold

units.summary: Bunching below the threshold is computed both in third-party-reported default liquid wealth, which individuals cannot manipulate, and in wealth including self-reported corrections, showing the excess mass is not a reporting artefact.
units.source_of_variation: the difference between two measures of the same concept for the same individuals: third-party-reported default liquid wealth versus reported liquid wealth including self-reported corrections

units.summary: The liquid-wealth notch is read off the density of total net wealth, which is not itself asset-tested, so excess mass there at the liquid-wealth threshold indicates real wealth reduction rather than portfolio reshuffling.
units.source_of_variation: the notch in the budget set created by the DKK 90,000 liquid-wealth asset test, read off the density of a broader wealth measure that is not itself asset-tested

units.summary: The 2010 discrete 15 percent rise in the asset test threshold, beyond standard wage indexation, shifts the location of the excess mass in the eligible group's wealth density, tying the bunching to the threshold itself.
units.source_of_variation: the discrete 15 percent increase in the asset test threshold in 2010, over and above the standard indexation to nominal average wages

units.summary: Monthly bank balances reveal excess mass below the threshold for eligible singles even outside December, relative to the flat monthly densities of the age-ineligible control group, showing year-round wealth suppression.
units.source_of_variation: high-frequency within-year variation in liquid wealth for a group exposed to an asset test evaluated on end-of-year liquid wealth, compared with an age-ineligible control group

units.summary: Because eligibility depends on end-of-December balances, the additional excess mass below the threshold in December relative to the average of the other ten months measures short-run timing responses, with the ineligible group showing no such pattern.
units.source_of_variation: the end-of-year timing of the asset test: within-year variation in the month at which liquid wealth is measured, for a group whose eligibility depends on end-of-December balances

units.summary: Excess mass below the notch survives when December bank balances are adjusted upward by all December cash withdrawals, an upper bound showing the bunching is not merely wealth hidden as cash.
units.source_of_variation: the notch created by the asset test, with the liquid wealth measure adjusted upward by all December cash withdrawals as an upper bound on cash-driven mismeasurement

units.summary: Low-income singles aged 60-64, who face no asset test because they are below the statutory retirement age, show no excess bunching and no within-year movement in their monthly bank wealth density, validating the counterfactual.
units.source_of_variation: a placebo group that faces no asset test: low-income singles aged 60-64, below the statutory retirement age, observed at monthly frequency

units.summary: Income-eligible but age-ineligible singles aged 60-64 face no asset test, and their December cash withdrawals show no threshold-specific excess, confirming the December withdrawal spike among the eligible is driven by the test.
units.source_of_variation: a placebo group facing no asset test: income-eligible singles aged 60-64, whose December cash withdrawals should show no threshold-specific excess

units.summary: Sons' log salaries are regressed on their own father's log salary and on the country-of-origin average of fathers' salaries (ethnic capital, interacted with origin group), with fixed effects for the father's municipality of residence at ages 35-40, so the intergenerational and ethnic-capital elasticities are identified from variation across father-son pairs within the same local labour market rath
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in fathers' salaries and in the country-of-origin average of fathers' salaries; within father's municipality of residence when he is aged 35-40.

units.summary: Within a cohort of children who followed the routine programme to 11 months, children are compared on hospitalisation hazards by their time-varying MMR-after-DTaP3 status, with age as timescale and measured covariates assumed to capture all confounding.
units.source_of_variation: Observational variation, within a cohort restricted to children who followed the DTaP/MMR programme to 11 months of age, in whether and when the child had received MMR after the third DTaP dose; vaccination status enters as a time-varying exposure with age as the underlying timescale.

units.summary: The same covariate-adjusted time-varying hazard comparison is run on DTaP3 versus DTaP2 status between 11 and 15 months, an exposure not expected to affect non-targeted infections, so any estimated hazard ratio gauges residual confounding in the main design.
units.source_of_variation: Observational variation, within the same restricted cohort between 11 and 15 months of age, in whether the child had received the third DTaP dose or only two doses — used as a negative control exposure to gauge bias rather than as a source of identifying variation.

units.summary: Households whose spouse dies of a fatal heart attack or stroke in a given year are compared with otherwise similar households whose spouse dies of the same cause five years later, and the treatment-by-post effect is allowed to differ by predetermined survivor characteristics (sex, presence of minor or adult children) and by whether the decedent was an earner.
units.source_of_variation: The calendar timing of a spouse's fatal heart attack or stroke (treatment versus control households whose spouse dies Δ = 5 years later), estimated separately for households in which the deceased spouse was an earner and in which the deceased was a nonearner, with the nonearner households reweighted to the age distribution of the earner households.

units.summary: Identification comes from the calendar timing of a spouse's fatal heart attack or stroke: households bereaved in year τ are differenced against households bereaved by the same cause in year τ+5, who are assigned a placebo event date at τ, so that within a five-year window the exact year of death is treated as as-good-as-random and trends would otherwise be parallel.
units.source_of_variation: The calendar timing of a spouse's fatal heart attack or stroke: households whose spouse has the fatal event in year τ (treatment) are compared with households whose spouse has the same type of fatal event in year τ + Δ, Δ = 5 (control), to whom a placebo event is assigned in year τ.

units.summary: Within the same bereaved-versus-later-bereaved difference-in-differences comparison, the household income loss caused by the death is instrumented by whether the deceased spouse had earnings and by a quadratic in that spouse's pre-event share of household income, so the mental-health response is attributed to the size of the income drop rather than to bereavement alone.
units.instrument: An indicator for whether the deceased spouse had earnings and a quadratic in the share of the household's income earned by the deceased spouse in the year before the event
units.source_of_variation: The calendar timing of a spouse's fatal heart attack or stroke (treatment versus control households whose spouse dies Δ = 5 years later), combined with variation in the share of household income earned by the deceased spouse at baseline, which is used to instrument the household's income loss.

units.summary: Identification comes from within-firm, over-time changes in how central the CEO, chair and board are in the national board-interlock network, with firm and year fixed effects plus CEO, workforce and firm controls assumed to absorb the remaining selection.
units.source_of_variation: Within-firm, over-time variation in the network coreness of the CEO, the Chair and the ordinary board members in the Danish population-scale board interlock network, net of firm and year fixed effects and of CEO, workforce and firm characteristics. No reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used.

units.summary: The same within-firm, over-time coreness variation is used in a model with a three-way interaction, so that the pay-premium effect of board coreness is compared across levels of chair coreness, net of firm and year fixed effects and controls.
units.source_of_variation: Within-firm, over-time variation in the network coreness of the CEO, the Chair and the ordinary board members, net of firm and year fixed effects and of CEO, workforce and firm characteristics; the quantity plotted is a pairwise comparison of marginal effects from a model that includes the three-way interaction.

units.summary: Volunteers are compared with non-volunteers in register-linked survey panel data, with identification resting on adjustment for rich observed confounders, 17 years of prior antidepressant-use history, birth-cohort and time-at-risk fixed effects and an individual random effect.
units.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used: the paper compares volunteers with non-volunteers (and intensities/organization types with non-volunteering) in observational DLSA data, adjusting for a rich set of register- and survey-based confounders -- most importantly 17 years of prior antidepressant-use history (1995-2003 and 2004-2011) -- plus birth-cohort and time-at-risk fixed effects and an individual-specific random effect

units.summary: Reported volunteering in one survey wave is related to mental health problems five years later, conditioning on baseline mental health problems and the study's other covariates so that remaining differences are attributed to volunteering.
units.source_of_variation: Observational variation in volunteering reported in the 2012 DLSA wave, with mental health problems in 2012 controlled for (lagged dependent variable)

units.summary: The effect is identified by contrasting the vaccination coverage of a birth cohort whose schedule fell entirely under the national reminder system with that of an earlier cohort that completed its vaccinations before the system existed, assuming no other cohort differences drive vaccination behaviour.
units.source_of_variation: Introduction of the proactive childhood vaccination reminder system in Denmark in August 2019: children born in January 2022 were covered by the system while children born in January 2018 completed all their vaccinations before it existed. The comparison is a before/after contrast of two national birth cohorts, with no concurrent comparison group.

units.summary: Each diagnosed child is matched to five undiagnosed classmates on school, grade, school year and sex, and absence rates are compared across periods around the index month with further covariate adjustment, so identification rests on the matched reference group being comparable conditional on observables.
units.source_of_variation: Matched cohort design on Danish register data: each child with JIA is matched to 5 reference children without a JIA diagnosis at the time of matching, matched on school, grade level, school year and sex, and school absence rates are compared between the two groups in each period relative to the index month. There is no reform, lottery or discontinuity - the comparison rests on matching plus covariate adjustment.

units.summary: Identification rests on cross-firm differences in the share of the workforce with tertiary education, assumed independent of unobserved innovation determinants once firm characteristics and industry dummies are controlled for, with an endogenous switching regression correcting only for firms' non-random selection into facing obstacles.
units.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation between firms in the share of their 2015 workforce with tertiary education, within 22 industries and conditional on firm characteristics. There is no reform, lottery or discontinuity; the endogenous switching regression (Lokshin & Sajaia, 2004) corrects only for the non-random selection of firms into the regime of facing obstacles, via a probit selection equation and an inverse Mills ratio.

units.summary: Among injured workers, whether a worker's vocational degree institutionally grants direct entry to a postsecondary programme shifts the probability of reskilling after the accident and is used as an instrument for reskilling's effect on later employment and disability insurance receipt.
units.instrument: Access to higher education upon injury (the worker's vocational degree grants direct entry to a higher degree)
units.source_of_variation: Institutional differences in the stackability of Danish vocational degrees: only a subset grants direct entry into postsecondary programs

units.summary: Outcome paths around the quasi-random date of a work accident are traced separately for workers whose vocational degree grants access to higher education and those whose degree does not, giving intention-to-treat effects of access and showing the two groups are comparable in injury severity and in pre-accident (placebo-event) enrolment.
units.source_of_variation: Institutional differences in the stackability of Danish vocational degrees: only a subset grants direct entry into postsecondary programs, interacted with the quasi-random timing of work accidents

units.summary: The date of a registered work accident causing loss of earning capacity is treated as quasi-random within occupation and observable characteristics, so earnings and education enrolment of injured workers around that date are compared with matched non-injured workers.
units.source_of_variation: Quasi-random timing of work accidents within occupations, 1995-2017 (AES Industrial Injury Register)

units.summary: Conditional on the other observed worker characteristics, variation in commuting distance to higher-education facilities at the time of injury is read as a determinant of whether injured workers reskill.
units.source_of_variation: Variation in workers' commuting distance to higher-education facilities upon injury

units.summary: Three cohorts passed the same school grades with different degrees of exposure to the 2020/21 closures, so the unexposed pre-pandemic cohort's grade-by-grade well-being trajectory serves as the counterfactual for the grade-by-cohort interactions of the exposed cohorts.
units.source_of_variation: COVID-19 pandemic and the Danish school closures of spring 2020 and winter 2020/2021: the early-pandemic cohort reached grade 9 after the onset of the pandemic, while the pre-pandemic cohort passed the same grade before it

units.summary: The slope linking ninth-grade well-being to upper-secondary track choice, conditional on exam GPA, is compared between the cohort that applied before the pandemic and the cohort that applied during it, so the cohort interaction carries the causal interpretation.
units.source_of_variation: Contrast between the pre-pandemic and early-pandemic cohorts in the slope of the well-being–track choice association; the early-pandemic cohort applied to upper secondary education during the pandemic

atlas.to_label: Enrolment in the academic upper-secondary track

units.summary: A pooled pandemic-exposure-by-grade interaction compares the well-being trajectories of the pandemic-exposed cohorts with those of the untreated pre-pandemic cohort over the same grade levels.
units.source_of_variation: COVID-19 pandemic and the Danish school closures of spring 2020 and winter 2020/2021, with the pre-pandemic cohort as the untreated group

units.summary: The same cohort contrast in the self-efficacy–track-choice slope is estimated without the GPA control, so the difference between pre-pandemic and early-pandemic applicants is identified from the raw conditional association across cohorts.
units.source_of_variation: Contrast between the pre-pandemic and early-pandemic cohorts in the slope of the academic-self-efficacy–track-choice association, without conditioning on GPA

units.summary: Historical pre-1994 enclave shares by occupation and origin, scaled by national immigrant stocks and mapped into workplace municipalities through historical native commuting flows, give establishments quasi-exogenous labor supply shocks that shift manager and production-worker wages separately, instrumenting establishment relative wages.
units.instrument: 𝐼𝑆𝐹 𝑀𝑗 — commuting-augmented immigration shock for managers in the establishment's workplace municipality j
units.source_of_variation: Commuting-augmented immigration share-shifter: pre-1994 occupation-country-municipality immigrant enclave shares combined with the log national stock of immigrants of that occupation and origin (leaving the municipality out), mapped from municipalities of residence into workplace municipalities with occupation-specific historical native commuting flows (Eqs. (18)-(19)). The 1986-1994 base period coincides with Denmark's quasi-random refugee dispersal policy.

units.summary: A Cobb-Douglas technology combining production workers with a distance-discounted managerial bundle is estimated jointly with labor supply equations, using the commuting-augmented immigration shocks to HQ-versus-establishment relative wages and the changing effect of establishment-HQ distance to pin down the elasticity of communication costs and the production parameters.
units.instrument: 𝐼𝑆𝐹 𝐿𝑘 − 𝐼𝑆𝐹 𝐿𝑗 and 𝐼𝑆𝐹 𝑀𝑘 − 𝐼𝑆𝐹 𝑀𝑗 (relative commuting-augmented immigration shocks for workers and for managers, HQ municipality k versus establishment municipality j), entered through the labor sup
units.source_of_variation: Commuting-augmented immigration share-shifters (Eqs. (18)-(19)) as labor supply shocks to relative wages, combined with variation in the distance between establishments and their HQ and in its effect over time, which identifies the distance elasticity of communication costs.

units.summary: For each married immigrant the year the spouse arrives in Denmark sets event time zero, and mental-health medication use is traced across event years relative to the year before arrival within the reunified population, so identification rests on outcomes evolving smoothly through the window absent the arrival rather than on any never-reunified control group.
units.source_of_variation: The timing of the spouse's arrival in Denmark under family reunification: for each married first-generation immigrant the year the spouse arrives defines event time 0, and outcomes are compared across event time within the reunified population, relative to the omitted year t-1. There is no never-reunified comparison group.

units.summary: Identification comes from changes within the same municipality over five-year periods in the composition of its immigrant and housing stocks, so that time-invariant municipality characteristics are differenced out and the remaining within-municipality variation (partly driven by national immigration, dispersal and housing reforms) identifies the effect of composition on segregation.
units.source_of_variation: Within-municipality variation over 1987-2015 in the composition of the immigrant and housing stocks, partly induced by the EU enlargement eastwards in 2004 and 2007, stricter immigration rules for asylum and family reunification since 2002, reduced passive income support, the Danish spatial dispersal policies on refugees (1986-1998 and 1999-2016) and the 1995 and 2004 reforms of public housing provision; five-year first differences remove time-invariant municipality characteristics.

units.summary: In a prospective cohort of routinely screened pregnant women, self-reported IPV exposure is compared with non-exposure on register-based birth outcomes, with identification resting on regression adjustment for a DAG-selected set of socio-demographic, behavioural and psychiatric covariates rather than on any exogenous shock.
units.source_of_variation: Observational variation in self-reported IPV among pregnant women routinely screened with the PROdata questionnaire in the STOP-VIO-PREG cohort; there is no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument - the design is a prospective cohort study with register-based outcomes.

units.summary: The 2009-10 reform's mechanical change in each worker's log net-of-tax rate, computed at baseline income, instruments the actual net-of-tax rate change (interacted with job switching) in a quadruple-difference specification that nets out mean reversion using pre-reform years and job stayers.
units.instrument: Δlog(1 − τ_it^sim), the simulated mechanical change in the log marginal net-of-tax rate holding individual income choices fixed at baseline values (Gruber and Saez 2002)
units.source_of_variation: The 2009–2010 Danish tax reform, which eliminated the middle tax bracket and raised the top-bracket threshold, cutting the marginal tax rate by 11.43 percentage points on average above a treatment threshold located at around the seventieth percentile of the income distribution and by 1.70 percentage points below it (a difference in tax treatment of 9.73 percentage points), combined with variation in job switching between firm × occupation cells.

units.instrument: Δlog(1 − τ_it^sim), the simulated mechanical change in the log marginal net-of-tax rate (Gruber and Saez 2002)
units.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which, like the 2009 reform, reduced tax rates at the top of the distribution relative to tax rates further down; only this reform among the four pre-2009 Danish reforms significantly changed the taxation of top earners relative to bottom and middle earners.

units.summary: Workers with baseline income above the reform threshold received a much larger marginal rate cut than those below, so comparing the two groups before and after 2009 identifies the reform's effect on job switching and on movers' earnings growth, with pre-reform differences netted out.
units.source_of_variation: The 2009–2010 Danish tax reform, which eliminated the middle tax bracket and raised the top-bracket threshold, cutting the marginal tax rate by 11.43 percentage points on average above a treatment threshold located at around the seventieth percentile of the income distribution and by 1.70 percentage points below it (a difference in tax treatment of 9.73 percentage points), combined with variation in job switching between firm × occupation cells.

units.summary: The 1987 reform's larger rate cut for high pre-reform incomes defines treated and control groups whose job-switching probabilities are compared before and after the reform.
units.source_of_variation: The 1987 Danish tax reform, which, like the 2009 reform, reduced tax rates at the top of the distribution relative to tax rates further down; only this reform among the four pre-2009 Danish reforms significantly changed the taxation of top earners relative to bottom and middle earners.

units.summary: Year-by-year coefficients for workers above versus below the reform threshold trace the path of job-switching probabilities (and switcher characteristics) around the 2009 reform date, with pre-reform coefficients used to assess parallel trends.
units.source_of_variation: The 2009–2010 Danish tax reform, which eliminated the middle tax bracket and raised the top-bracket threshold, cutting the marginal tax rate by 11.43 percentage points on average above a treatment threshold located at around the seventieth percentile of the income distribution and by 1.70 percentage points below it (a difference in tax treatment of 9.73 percentage points), combined with variation in job switching between firm × occupation cells.

units.summary: Earnings and hours of workers promoted within their firm are followed quarter by quarter relative to the promotion date against unpromoted coworkers in the same firm at the same event time, documenting the dynamic earnings path around a job-ladder step.
units.source_of_variation: Within-firm promotions, defined as switches to an occupation cell with at least 10 percent higher median earnings, compared with unpromoted coworkers in the same firm at the same event time.

units.summary: The estimated reform effect on movers' earnings growth is plotted by years elapsed since the 2009 reform, with pre-reform bracket instrumenting actual bracket, so the dynamics of the response of job switchers are read off the post-reform event-time profile.
units.instrument: pre-reform tax bracket, used as an instrument for actual post-reform tax bracket in the treatment-on-the-treated series (Panel B)
units.source_of_variation: The 2009–2010 Danish tax reform, which eliminated the middle tax bracket and raised the top-bracket threshold, cutting the marginal tax rate by 11.43 percentage points on average above a treatment threshold located at around the seventieth percentile of the income distribution and by 1.70 percentage points below it (a difference in tax treatment of 9.73 percentage points), combined with variation in job switching between firm × occupation cells.
